qo/as.head: Θόας-1
qo/as.html:
Θόας-1 (Αἰτωλός). Patronymic Ἀνδραιμονίδης. Son of Andraemon and leader of the Aetolians Il. 2.638 ; slays Peiroos Il. 4.527 , 529; accepts Hector's challenge but does not get the lot Il. 7.168; Il. 13.92; Poseidon takes his guise Il. 13.216, 222, 228; Thoas advises the chiefs to stand up to Hector, sending the general body back Il. 15.281; Il. 19.239: in Odysseus's tale to Eumaeus and his companions Od. 14.499.
Θόας-2 (θεῖος). King of Lemnos Il. 14.230, Il. 23.745.
Θόας-3 Trojan. killed by Menelaus Il. 16.311.

qu/on.head: θύον
qu/on.html: θύον τό. A tree not identified, the wood of which emits (sweet) odour when burnt Od. 5.60.

qa/lassa.head: θάλασσα
qa/lassa.html: θάλασσα -ης, ἡ. 1 The sea: πολυφλοίσβοιο θαλάσσης Il. 1.34. Cf. Il. 1.157, 437, 496, Il. 2.159, 294, Il. 4.248, etc.: πεφευγότες θάλασσαν Od. 1.12. Cf. Od. 1.50, 52, Od. 2.260, 407, Od. 3.142, Od. 4.435, 501, 504, Od. 5.401, 413, 418, Od. 6.95, 272, etc. 2 Distinguished in terms from the land: γαίης νέρθε καὶ θαλάσσης Il. 14.204. Cf. Il. 8.24. From the land and the heavens Il. 18.483: Od. 12.404 = Od. 14.302. From other waters Il. 21.196. 3 Personified: γλαυκή σε τίκτε θ. Il. 16.34. 4 Sea-water: θ. κήκιε πολλή Od. 5.455. Cf. Il. 10.572.

quo/w.head: †θυόω
quo/w.html: †θυόω [θύος. Cf. θυήεις, θυόεις.] Neut. pf. pple, pass. τεθυωμένον. To impart fragrance to: ἐλαίῳ, τό ῥά οἱ τεθυωμένον ἦεν (which she had by her in (full) fragrance) Il. 14.172.

qh=bai.head: Θῆβαι-1
qh=bai.html:
Θῆβαι-1 Θήβη-1 Il. 4.378, 406, Il. 14.323, Il. 19.99: Od. 11.263, 265, 275 (ἑπτάπυλος, εὐρύχορος , ἐϋστέφανος, ἱερὰ τείχεα , πολυήρατος). The Boeotian city, traditionally said to have been founded by Cadmus (represented as having been founded by Amphion-2 and Zethus Od. 11.262) Il. 4.378, 406, Il. 5.804, Il. 6.223, Il. 10.286, Il. 14.114, 323, Il. 19.99: Od. 11.263, 265, 275, Od. 15.247. Θήβασδε [-δε], to Thebes-1 Il. 23.679 .
Θῆβαι-2 (ἑκατόμπυλοι). The city of Upper Egypt Il. 9.381: Od. 4.126.

qwh/.head: θωή
qwh/.html: θωή -ῆς, ἡ. 1 A fine or penalty: σοὶ θωὴν ἐπιθήσομεν Od. 2.192. 2 Specifically, a fine in place of personal service in war: ἀργαλέην θωὴν ἀλέεινεν Ἀχαιῶν Il. 13.669 (cf. Il. 23.296).

qumofqo/ros.head: θυμοφθόρος
qumofqo/ros.html: θυμοφθόρος [θυμός + φθορ-, φθείρω.] Life-destroying: φάρμακα (poisons) Od. 2.329, ἄχος (heart-breaking, crushing) Od. 4.716, κάματον (that crushes the spirit) Od. 10.363, ὅς κε τοῦτον ἀνίαζῃ θ. (molesting or annoying beyond endurance) Od. 19.323. Absol.: γράψας ἐν πίνακι θυμοφθόρα πολλά (much matter that was to be his death-warrant) Il. 6.169.

qe/rw.head: θέρω
qe/rw.html: θέρω Fut. pple. mid. θερσόμενος Od. 19.507. Aor. subj. pass. θερέω Od. 17.23. 1 In mid., to warm oneself: φόως ἔμεν ἠδὲ θέρεσθαι Od. 19.64. Cf. Od. 19.507. 2 In pass., to be warmed: ἐπεί κε πυρὸς θερέω (genit. of material) Od. 17.23. To be burnt: μὴ ἄστυ πυρὸς θέρηται Il. 6.331. Cf. Il. 11.667.

qrasu/s.head: θρασύς
qrasu/s.html: θρασύς -εῖα [cf. θράσος.] 1 Bold, stout: ἡνίοχον Il. 8.89, 126, ἡνιοχῆα 312. Epithet of Hector Il. 12.60 = 210, Il. 13.725, Il. 22.455, Il. 24.72, 786. Of other heroes Il. 8.128, Il. 16.604: Od. 10.436. 2 Of hands, stout, strong Il. 11.553 = Il. 17.662, Il. 11.571, Il. 13.134, Il. 15.314, Il. 23.714: Od. 5.434. 3 Epithet of war, carried on with spirit, strenous Il. 6.254, Il. 10.28: Od. 4.146.

qrasume/mnwn.head: θρασυμέμνων
qrasume/mnwn.html: θρασυμέμνων -ονος [θρασύς + μεμ-, μάω.] Of bold spirit, stout of heart Il. 5.639: Od. 11.267.

qe/aina.head: θέαινα
qe/aina.html: θέαινα ἡ [fem. as θεά. Cf. λέαινα, lioness.] A goddess as distinguished from a god: πάντες τε θεοὶ πᾶσαί τε θέαιναι Il. 8.5 = Il. 19.101, Il. 8.20. Cf. Od. 8.341.

qarsale/os.head: θαρσαλέος
qarsale/os.html: θαρσαλέος -η, -ον [θάρσος.] 1 Bold, stout, courageous, spirited, confident: πολεμιστήν Il. 5.602 = Il. 16.493 = Il. 22.269. Cf. Il. 19.169, Il. 21.430, 589: Od. 7.51. Neut. comp. θαρσαλεώτερον in impers. construction: θ. ἔσται (one would feel more confidence, have better heart) Il. 10.223. 2 Over-bold, audacious, presuming: θαρσαλέος τις προΐκτης Od. 17.449. Cf. Od. 19.91.

qauma/zw.head: θαυμάζω
qauma/zw.html: θαυμάζω [θαῦμα.] 3 pl. pa. iterative θαυμάζεσκον Od. 19.229. 3 sing. fut. in mid. form θαυμάσσεται Il. 18.467. (ἀπο-.) 1 To wonder, marvel, to feel or be struck with wonder, astonishment or admiration: γυναῖκες ἱστάμεναι θαύμαζον Il. 18.496. Cf. Il. 24.394: θαύμαζεν ὁ γεραιός Od. 3.373. Cf. Od. 4.44, Od. 7.145, Od. 8.265, Od. 13.157, Od. 16.203. With dependent clause: θαυμάζομεν οἷον ἐτύχθη Il. 2.320. 2 To wonder or marvel at, look upon with wonder or eager curiousity: πτόλεμόν τε μάχην τε Il. 13.11. Cf. Il. 10.12, Il. 18.467: λιμένας καὶ νῆας Od. 7.43. Cf. Od. 1.382 = Od. 18.411 = Od. 20.269, Od. 4.655, Od. 9.153, Od. 19.229, Od. 24.370. With infin.: οἷον θαυμάζομεν (impf.) Ἕκτορα αἰχμητὴν ἔμεναι (thinking that he was . . .) Il. 5.601. To look upon or behold (a person) with respectful wonder and admiration: Πρίαμος θαύμαζʼ Ἀχιλῆα Il. 24.629. Cf. Il. 24.631: Od. 8.459.

qe/eion.head: θέειον
qe/eion.html: θέειον -ου, τό. Also θήϊον Od. 22.493. Sulphur. 1 In reference to the sulphurous smell associated with a thunderbolt: δεινὴ θεείου γίγνεται ὀδμή Il. 14.415. Cf. Il. 8.135: Od. 12.417, Od. 14.307. 2 Used for cleansing by fumigation: ἐκάθηρε θεείῳ Il. 16.228. Cf. Od. 22.481, 493.

qrwsmo/s.head: θρωσμός
qrwsmo/s.html: θρωσμός [θρῴσκω.] Only in phrase ἐπὶ θρωσμῷ πεδίοιο, a piece of ground rising from, and somewhat above the general level of, the plainIl. 10.160, Il. 11.56 = Il. 20.3.

qruli/ssw.head: †θρυλίσσω
qruli/ssw.html: †θρυλίσσω (ῡ) 3 sing. aor. pass. θρῡλίχθη. To crush, bruise: θρυλίχθη μέτωπον Il. 23.396.

qro/nion.head: Θρόνιον
qro/nion.html: Θρόνιον A Locrian town Il. 2.533.

qei/nw.head: θείνω
qei/nw.html: θείνω 3 sing. aor. ἔθεινε Il. 21.491. θεῖνε Il. 16.339. 3 sing. subj. θείνῃ Od. 18.63. Pple. θείνας Il. 20.481. To strike, smite: μή σε ἴδωμαι θεινομένην Il. 1.588. Cf. Il. 6.135, Il. 10.484, Il. 16.339, Il. 17.430, Il. 20.481, Il. 21.21, 491: ὅς κέ σε θείνῃ Od. 18.63. Cf. Od. 9.459, Od. 22.443.

qu/nw.head: θύνω
qu/nw.html: θύνω [θύω1.] To run, run about, rush Il. 2.446, Il. 5.87, 96, 250, Il. 10.524, Il. 11.73, 188 = 203, 342 = Il. 20.412, Il. 11.570, Il. 20.493: Od. 24.449.

qumarh/s.head: θυμαρής
qumarh/s.html: θυμαρής -ές [θυμός + ἀρ-, ἀραρίσκω. Fitted to the heart.] Neut. in form θυμῆρες Od. 10.362. 1 Such as to inspire affection, lovely, beauteous: ἄλοχον Il. 9.336: Od. 23.232. 2 Suited to one's taste, grateful to the senses: [ὕδωρ] θυμῆρες κεράσασα (till it became. . .) Od. 10.362. 3 Suited to one's needs, serviceable: σκῆπρον Od. 17.199.

qeo/s.head: θεός
qeo/s.html: θεός -οῦ, ὁ, ἡ. Instrumental θεόφιν. With a word expressing likeness Il. 7.366, Il. 14.318, Il. 17.477: Od. 3.110, 409. This form as ablative Il. 17.101, Il. 23.347. 1 A divine being, a god Il. 1.28, Il. 2.318, Il. 3.230, Il. 5.177, Il. 8.200, Il. 14.168, Il. 16.531, Il. 19.3, Il. 22.10, Il. 24.460, etc.: Od. 1.323, Od. 2.5, Od. 4.236, Od. 8.177, Od. 12.88, Od. 17.475, Od. 19.396, Od. 21.258, Od. 24.445, etc. 2 A god as distinguished in terms from a goddess: εἰρωτᾷς με θεὰ θεόν Od. 5.97. Cf. Il. 10.50. From a mortal: ἠμὲν θεὸν ἠδὲ καὶ ἄνδρα Il. 5.128. Cf. Il. 19.417, Il. 22.9, Il. 24.259, etc.: Od. 4.397, 654, etc. 3 Without reference to any particular god, the divine power, heaven: θεός που σοὶ τό γʼ ἔδωκεν Il. 1.178. Cf. Il. 2.436, Il. 6.228, Il. 7.4, Il. 9.49, Il. 17.327, Il. 21.47, etc.: οὐκ ἄνευ θεοῦ Od. 2.372. Cf. Od. 3.131, Od. 8.170, Od. 9.158. Od. 11.292, Od. 17.399, Od. 18.265, etc. 4 A goddess Il. 1.516, Il. 3.381, Il. 4.58, Il. 5.331, 339, 839, Il. 6.380 = 385, Il. 8.7, Il. 18.394, Il. 24.223: Od. 1.420, Od. 2.297, 406 = Od. 3.30 = Od. 5.193 = Od. 7.38, Od. 4.831 (twice), Od. 5.194, 459, Od. 6.149, 150, Od. 7.41, 71, 246, 255, Od. 8.467 = Od. 15.181, Od. 10.136 = Od. 11.8 = Od. 12.150, Od. 10.297, Od. 12.449, Od. 13.189, Od. 20.47. 5 A goddess as distinguished in terms from a woman: ἢ θεὸς ἠὲ γυνή Od. 10.228, 255. 6 In pl., the gods: τίς θεῶν; Il. 1.8, θεοί μοι αἴτιοί εἰσιν Il. 3.164. Cf. Il. 1.18, Il. 2.321, Il. 4.1, Il. 6.138, Il. 7.360, Il. 9.485, Il. 12.8, etc.: Od. 1.17, Od. 2.66, Od. 4.379, Od. 5.335, Od. 7.132, Od. 11.276, Od. 12.394, etc. 7 In pl., the gods as distinguished in terms from the goddesses: πάντες τε θεοὶ πᾶσαί τε θέαιναι Il. 8.5 = Il. 19.101, Il. 8.20. Cf. Od. 8.341. From mortals: πρός τε θεῶν πρός τʼ ἀνθρώπων Il. 1.339. Cf. Il. 1.403, Il. 9.239, Il. 14.233, Il. 21.264, etc.: Od. 1.338, Od. 2.211, Od. 16.265, Od. 24.64, etc.

qumoi/ths.head: Θυμοίτης
qumoi/ths.html: Θυμοίτης A Trojan elder Il. 3.146 .

qoo/w.head: θοόω
qoo/w.html: θοόω [poss. conn. with θοός and meaning orig. to make quick or active, acquiring the sense of sharpening when applied to weapons, etc..] To sharpen, put a point upon: ἐθόωσα [ῥόπαλον.] i 327.

qre/ptra.head: θρέπτρα
qre/ptra.html: θρέπτρα τά [θρεπ-, τρέφω.] Recompense for rearing due by a child to his parents: οὐδὲ τοκεῦσι θ. ἀπέδωκεν Il. 4.478 = Il. 17.302.

qe/sfatos.head: θέσφατος
qe/sfatos.html: θέσφατος -ον [the second element φα-, φημί. The first explained as θεσ-, θεός.] 1 Pronounced or ordained by a god or by the divine will. Neut. in impers. construction: ὡς γὰρ θέσφατόν ἐστιν Il. 8.477. With infin.: θανέειν Od. 4.561. Cf. Od. 10.473. 2 Absol. in neut. pl. θέσφατα, divine ordinances or decrees: οὔ τι θεῶν ἐκ θ. ᾔδη Il. 5.64. Cf. Od. 9.507 = Od. 13.172, Od. 11.151, 297, Od. 12.155. 3 = θεσπέσιος 4..b: ἀήρ Od. 7.143.

qa/lpios.head: Θάλπιος
qa/lpios.html: Θάλπιος See Ἀκτορίων. Son of Eurytus-2 and grandson of Poseidon. A leader of the Epeians Il. 2.620.

qumalgh/s.head: θυμαλγής
qumalgh/s.html: θυμαλγής [θυμός + ἄλγας.] Paining or burdening the heart, painful, distressing, grievous Il. 4.513, Il. 9.260, 387, 565: Od. 8.272, Od. 16.69, Od. 18.347 = Od. 20.285, Od. 20.118, Od. 22.189, Od. 23.64, 183, Od. 24.326.

qea/.head: θεά
qea/.html: θεά -ᾶς, ἡ [fem. of θεός.] Dat. pl. θεῇσι Il. 8.305. Il. 11.638, Il. 19.286: Od. 7.291. θεῇς Il. 3.158. θεαῖς Od. 5.119. 1 A female divine (or semi-divine) being, a goddess: εἰ θεά σε γείνατο μήτηρ Il. 1.280 (Thetis). Cf. Il. 1.1, Il. 2.182, Il. 3.396, Il. 8.305, Il. 18.429, etc.: καλυψώ, δῖα θεάων Od. 1.14, θεά οἱ ἔκλυεν ἀρῆς Od. 4.767 (Athene). Cf. Od. 2.392, Od. 5.215, Od. 10.222, Od. 12.131, Od. 20.393, etc. 2 A goddess as distinguished in terms from a god: εἰρωτᾷς με θεὰ θεόν Od. 5.97. Cf. Il. 10.50. From a woman: θεᾶς οὐδὲ γυναικός Il. 14.315. 3 With the name of a particular goddess. With Ἥρη Il. 1.55, Il. 5.711, Il. 8.350, etc. With Ἀθήνη Il. 1.206, Il. 2.166, Il. 5.405, etc.: Od. 1.44, Od. 2.382, Od. 3.13, etc. With Ἠώς Il. 2.48. With Θέτις Il. 9.410, Il. 15.76, Il. 18.127, etc. With Θέμις Il. 15.93. With Ἶρις Il. 15.206, Il. 18.182. With Ἐρινύς Od. 15.234.

quo/eis.head: θυόεις
quo/eis.html: θυόεις -εν [θύος. Cf. θυήεις.] Sweet-smelling, fragrant: θυόεν νέφος Il. 15.153.

qeopro/pos.head: θεοπρόπος
qeopro/pos.html: θεοπρόπος [app., one who prays to a god, fr. θεός + προπ-, perh. conn. with L. precor.] One who reveals the divine will, a seer Il. 12.228: Od. 1.416. Joined with οἰωνιστής Il. 13.70.

qairo/s.head: θαιρός
qairo/s.html: θαιρός ὁ. App. vertical (presumably metal) pegs at the top and bottom of a side of a gate working in stone sockets and governing the opening and shutting Il. 12.459.

qa/lamos.head: θάλαμος
qa/lamos.html: θάλαμος -ου, ὁ. A room or chamber. 1 a A sleeping-chamber, a bed-room: πρόσθεν θαλάμοιο θυράων Il. 9.473 (app. a room built in the αὐλή and opening into the αἴθουσα near the πρόδομος; or perh. a portion of the αἴθουσα next the πρόδομος walled off). Cf. Il. 9.475: ὅθι οἱ θ. αὐλῆς δέδμητο Od. 1.425 (αὐλῆς app. local genit., in the . . . ; cf. Il. 9.473 above), ἐς θάλαμον ᾧ ἔνι κούρη κοιμᾶτο Od. 6.15. Cf. Od. 1.436, 441, Od. 2.5 = Od. 4.310, Od. 3.413, Od. 7.7, Od. 10.340, Od. 19.48. b A bridal chamber: γήμας ἐκ θαλάμοιο μετὰ κλέος ἵκετʼ Ἀχαιῶν (leaving his just wedded wife) Il. 11.227. c The sleeping-chamber occupied by a married pair: θάλαμον λιποῦσα (i.e. the bed of Menclaus) Il. 3.174. Cf. Il. 3.382, 391, 423, Il. 6.244, 248, Il. 9.582, 588, Il. 17.36: νοσφισσαμένην θάλαμόν τε πόσιν τε Od. 4.263. Cf. Od. 23.178, 192, 229, 295. Of such a room in the palace of Zeus Il. 14.166, 188, 338. In the palace of Hephaestus Od. 8.277. 2 A chamber appropriated to the lady of a house and her maidens: ὡρμᾶτʼ ἐκ θαλάμοιο Il. 3.142 (the same as the μέγαρον of 125). Cf. Il. 6.316, 321, 336: ἐξ Ἑλένη θαλάμοιο ἤλυθεν Od. 4.121. Cf. Od. 4.718, 802, Od. 17.36 = Od. 19.53, Od. 17.506. In pl. of the women's apartments generally: νύμφας ἐκ θαλάμων ἠγίνεον Il. 18.492 (cf. Od. 22.143 cited under (4); or this may be the pl. of indefiniteness like νύμφας in this line and γάμοι and εἰλαπίναι in the prec. line) (u.l. ἐς θαλάμους, which would go under 1.b): μυχῷ θαλάμων ἥμεθα Od. 23.41. 3 A work-room Il. 4.143. 4 A room for storage or safe custody, a store-room, a treasure-chamber: θύρη θαλάμοιο ἀνέρος ἀφνειοῖο Il. 24.317: χηλὸν ἐξέφερεν θαλάμοιο Od. 8.439, ἀνέβαινε ἐς θαλάμους Od. 22.143 (app. meaning a single room; cf. Il. 18.492 cited under (3)). Cf. Il. 6.288, Il. 22.63, Il. 24.191, 275: Od. 2.337, Od. 3.441, Od. 6.74, Od. 15.99, Od. 16.285, Od. 19.17, 256, Od. 21.42, Od. 22.140, 155, 157, 166, 174, 179, 180, Od. 24.166.

qelkth/rion.head: θελκτήριον
qelkth/rion.html: θελκτήριον τό [θέλγω.] 1 A means of enchantment, a spell Il. 14.215. 2 A means of propitiating or placating: θεῶν θελκτήριον Od. 8.509. 3 Something that charms or delights Od. 1.337.

qera/pwn.head: θεράπων
qera/pwn.html: θεράπων -οντος, ὁ. 1 A follower, retainer or henchman: θεράποντες ἀπʼ ὤμων τεύχεʼ ἕλοντο Il. 7.122. Cf. Il. 1.321, Il. 5.48, Il. 6.53, Il. 11.843, Il. 13.600, Il. 15.401, Il. 16.272 = Il. 17.165, Il. 19.143, 281, Il. 24.396, 406, 573: ἴσθμιον ἤνεικεν θ. Od. 18.300. Cf. Od. 1.109, Od. 4.23 = 217, Od. 4.38, 784, Od. 16.253, 326 = 360, Od. 18.297, 424. Fig. of warriors: θεράποντες Ἄρηος Il. 2.110 = Il. 6.67 = Il. 15.733 = Il. 19.78. Cf. Il. 7.382, Il. 8.79, Il. 10.228, Il. 19.47. Of kings θεράποντε διός Od. 11.255. 2 A warrior in honourable personal attendance on another, the relation of the two resembling generally that of squire and knight: ἠῢς θ. Ἀχιλῆος (Patroclus) Il. 16.653. Cf. Il. 7.149, Il. 11.322, 620, Il. 13.246, 331, Il. 15.431, Il. 16.165 = Il. 17.388, Il. 16.244, 279, 464, 865, Il. 17.164, 271, Il. 18.152, Il. 23.90, 113 = 124, 528, 860 = 888. 3 Applied to a warrior's ἡνίοχος: ἵππους θ. ἀπάνευθʼ ἔχεν Il. 4.227, ἡνίοχον θεράποντα Il. 5.580. Cf. Il. 6.18, Il. 8.104, 109, 113, 119, Il. 11.341, 488, Il. 12.76, 111, Il. 13.386, Il. 20.487.

qu/ella.head: θύελλα
qu/ella.html: θύελλα -ης, ἡ [θύω1.] 1 A rushing or violent wind or storm: φλογὶ ἶσοι ἠὲ θυέλλῃ Il. 13.39. Cf. Il. 6.346, Il. 12.253, Il. 15.26, Il. 21.335: ἀναρπάξασά μιν θ. θέρεν Od. 4.515, Od. 23.316. Cf. Od. 4.727, Od. 5.317, 419, Od. 6.171, Od. 7.275, Od. 10.48, 54, Od. 12.288, 409, Od. 20.63, 66. 2 Of a dust-storm: κονίη ἵσταθʼ ὥς τε νέφος ἠὲ θ. Il. 23.366. App. of volcanic fire: πυρὸς ὀλοοῖο θύελλαι Od. 12.68.

qei=os.head: θεῖος
qei=os.html: θεῖος -η, -ον [θεός.] 1 Partaking of the nature of the gods, divine, immortal: θείοιο γέροντος (Proteus) Od. 4.395. 2 Consisting of gods: ἀγῶνα (see ἀγών 1.a) Il. 7.298, Il. 18.376. 3 Connected with the gods, sacred: ἁλός Il. 9.214 (perh. as used for purifying sacrifices): χορόν Od. 8.264 (app. from the dance being regarded as a matter of ritual). 4 Of divine origin, from a divine source, divine: Ὄνειρος Il. 2.22, 56, ὀμφή Il. 2.41, γένος Il. 6.180, πύργου Il. 21.526 (app. as god-built; see 446 and cf. Il. 7.452, Il. 8.519): ὄνειρος Od. 14.495. Applied to persons of divine descent: Ἴλου Il. 10.415 (he was descended from Zeus; see Il. 20.215-232), Ἡρακλῆος Il. 15.25, Il. 20.145, ἀνδρὸς θείοιο Ἀχιλλῆος Il. 16.798, Πηλεΐδαο Il. 17.199, Ἀχιλλῆος Il. 19.279, 297: Ἐνιπῆος Od. 11.238 (since all rivers spring from Zeus). 5 Applied to kings as holding their office from Zeus Od. 4.621, 691, Od. 16.335. To heralds as under his special protection Il. 4.192, Il. 10.315. To bards as singing by divine inspiration Il. 18.604: = Od. 4.17, Od. 1.336, Od. 8.43, 47, 87, 539, Od. 13.27, Od. 16.252, Od. 17.359, Od. 23.133, 143, Od. 24.439. 6 Applied as a mere epithet of honour to Odysseus Il. 2.335, Il. 9.218, Il. 10.243, Il. 11.806: Od. 1.65, Od. 2.233, 259, Od. 3.398, Od. 4.682, etc. To Oïleus Il. 13.694 = Il. 15.333. To Thoas Il. 14.230. To Munes Il. 19.296. 7 Denoting a superlative degree of excellence or beauty: ποτόν Od. 2.341, Od. 9.205, δόμον Od. 4.43.

qumbrai=os.head: Θυμβραῖος
qumbrai=os.html: Θυμβραῖος Trojan. killed by Diomedes Il. 11.320.

qumo/s.head: θυμός
qumo/s.html: θυμός -οῦ, ὁ. The heart, breast, soul, mind (cf. ἦτορ, καρδίη, κραδίη, κῆρ, φρήν). I As the seat or a seat (when coupled with φρήν, φρένες, κραδίη hardly to be distinguished therefrom) 1 Of life; hence a Vitality, the vital powers, strength (cf. ἦτορ 2.a.α, κῆρ 2.a): ὀλίγος ἔτι θ. ἐνῆεν Il. 1.593. Cf. Il. 3.294 (of sacrificial victims), Il. 4.152, Il. 14.439, Il. 15.240, Il. 16.540, Il. 20.472, Il. 21.417, Il. 22.475: εἰς ὅ κεν αὖτις θυμὸν λάβητε Od. 10.461. Cf. Od. 5.458, Od. 10.78, Od. 19.263, Od. 24.349. b The animating principle, the vital spirit, the soul, the life, life, one's life (cf. αἰών 3, ἦτορ 2.a.β, μένος 7, ψυχή 1): τάχʼ ἂν θυμὸν ὀλέσσῃ Il. 1.205. Cf. Il. 4.524, 531, Il. 5.155, 317, 673, 698, Od. 11.334, Il. 12.150 (of wild boars), Il. 17.17, Il. 21.296, etc.: κεκαφηότα θυμόν Od. 5.468. Cf.Od. 11.201, 203, Od. 12.350, Od. 13.270, Od. 14.405, Od. 15.354, Od. 17.236, Od. 20.62, Od. 21.154, 171, Od. 22.388 (of fishes), 462. c The spirit or soul thought of as distinct from the body and as leaving it at death (cf. ψυχή 4): θ. ᾤχετʼ ἀπὸ μελέων Il. 13.671 = Il. 16.606. Cf. Il. 4.470, Il. 7.131, Il. 12.386, Il. 16.469 (of a horse), 743, Il. 20.406, Il. 23.880 (of a bird): λίπʼ ὀστέα θ. Od. 3.455 (of a sacrificial victim), Od. 12.414. Cf. Od. 10.163 (of a deer) = Od. 19.454 (of a wild boar), Od. 11.221. 2 Of spirit, courage, stoutness, resolution, endurance: ὅν τινα θ. ἐμοὶ μαχέσασθαι ἀνώγει Il. 7.74. Cf. Il. 1.228, Il. 2.276, Il. 3.9, Il. 4.289, Il. 5.470, Il. 6.439, Il. 10.205, Il. 13.73, 487, Il. 15.321, Il. 17.68, Il. 22.252, etc.: ἀέξεταί μοι θ. Od. 2.315. Cf. Od. 1.320, 353, Od. 4.447, 459, 713, Od. 5.222, Od. 9.435, Od. 11.181 = Od. 16.37, Od. 16.99, Od. 17.284, Od. 18.61, 135, Od. 23.100 = 168, Od. 24.163, 511. In reference to animals or insects Il. 12.300 (a lion), Il. 13.704 (oxen). Cf. Il. 16.162, 266, etc. 3 a Of anger, wrath, indignation: θυμὸν χολώθη (in his heart) Il. 4.494, Il. 13.660, ἀπειλήσω τό γε θυμῷ (from my heart, in earnest) Il. 15.212. Cf. Il. 1.192, 217, 243, 429, Il. 2.196, 223, Il. 6.326, Il. 9.109, 255, 436, 496, 587, 629, 635, 675, Il. 14.50, 207 = 306, Il. 15.155, Il. 16.206, 616, Il. 18.113 = Il. 19.66, Il. 19.271, Il. 20.29: μὴ χόλον ἔνθεο θυμῷ Od. 24.248. Cf. Od. 7.306, Od. 11.562, Od. 20.266. Hence, anger, wrath: σοὶ ἄλληκτον θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσι θεοὶ θέσαν Il. 9.637. Cf. Od. 13.148. Evil passions: ὑμέτερος θ. καὶ ἀεικέα ἔργα φαίνεται Od. 4.694. b Of madness, rage, fury, wild excitement: ἀλύσσοντες περὶ θυμῷ Il. 22.70 (of dogs) (see Il. 21.65, etc., under 4.a). Cf. Il. 23.468: Od. 21.302. 4 a Of desire, longing, appetite: ἵμερον ἔμβαλε θυμῷ Il. 3.139, περὶ δʼ ἤθελε θυμῷ . . . Il. 21.65, Il. 24.236 (περί advbl., exceedingly in his heart; cf. Il. 22.70 under 3.b and Od. 14.146 under (6)), αἲ γάρ με μένος καὶ θ. ἀνείη . . . (desire for vengeance) Il. 22.346. Cf. Il. 1.468 = 602 = Il. 2.431 = Il. 7.320 = Il. 23.56, Il. 2.589, Il. 4.263, Il. 8.301 = 310, 322, Il. 9.177, Il. 10.401, Il. 13.386, Il. 16.255, Il. 18.176, Il. 20.77, Il. 21.177, Il. 24.198, 288: ἐπεὶ ἔπιον ὅσον ἤθελε θ. Od. 3.342 = 395 = Od. 7.184 = 228 = Od. 18.427, Od. 21.273. Cf. Od. 2.248, Od. 5.95 = Od. 14.111, Od. 8.70, 98, 450, Od. 11.105, 206, 566, Od. 13.40, Od. 14.28, 46, Od. 15.66, Od. 16.141, 479 = Od. 19.425, Od. 17.603, Od. 18.164, Od. 19.198, 343, Od. 23.257. In reference to animals Il. 8.189 (of horses), Il. 22.142 (of a hawk). One's wishes or liking: ἄρσαντες κατὰ θυμόν Il. 1.136. Cf. Il. 9.645. b Of the sexual impulse: τῇ θυμὸν ὄρινεν (sought to excite . . .) Il. 3.395. Cf. Il. 14.316: ᾧ θυμῷ εἴξασα μίγη . . . Od. 5.126. Cf. Od. 18.212. 5 Of volition: οὐκ Ἀτρεΐδῃ ἥνδανε θυμῷ Il. 1.24 = 378, εἴ τοι θ. ἐπέσσυται Il. 1.173, ἑκὼν ἀέκοντί γε θυμῷ Il. 4.43. Cf. Il. 5.676, Il. 7.68, Il. 8.39, Il. 9.398, Il. 10.534, Il. 12.174, Il. 18.90, Il. 20.32, Il. 21.386, Il. 22.78, etc.: ἐπεπείθετο θ. Od. 2.103, τελέσαι με θ. ἄνωγεν Od. 5.89. Cf. Od. 4.140, Od. 7.187, 258, Od. 8.45, Od. 13.145, Od. 14.445, Od. 18.409, Od. 21.194, etc. In reference to animals: οὐδὲ λύκοι τε καὶ ἄρνες ὁμόφρονα θυμὸν ἔχουσιν Il. 22.263. Cf. Il. 10.531 = Il. 11.520 (horses). Inclination, a mind: ἐπεί τοι θ. [ἐστιν] αἰτιάασθαι Il. 13.775. Cf. Il. 20.349. 6 Of feelings, emotions, moods, such as joy, grief, affection, dislike, pity, hope, fear, resentment, reverence, regard, solicitude, wonder, etc.: θυμῷ φιλέουσα Il. 1.196 = 209, κεχαροίατό κε θυμῷ 256, ἄχος κραδίην καὶ θυμὸν ἵκανεν Il. 2.171, σεβάσσατο τό γε θυμῷ Il. 6.167, 417. Cf. Il. 2.142, Il. 3.438, Il. 4.208, Il. 7.189, Il. 8.138, Il. 9.8, 343 (from the bottom of my heart), 639, Il. 10.69, 355, Il. 13.82, 163, Il. 14.104, Il. 15.561, Il. 17.254, 625, Il. 19.229, Il. 21.456, Il. 23.62, etc.: θάμβησεν κατὰ θυμόν Od. 1.323, δ οὔ ποτε ἔλπετο θυμῷ Od. 3.275, κότον ἔνθετο θυμῷ Od. 11.102, δείσασʼ ἐνὶ θυμῷ Od. 16.331. Cf. Od. 1.4, Od. 2.79, 138, Od. 4.71, Od. 5.83, Od. 8.15 (their curiosity), Od. 10.63, 248, Od. 11.39, Od. 14.146 (see Il. 21.65, etc., under 4.a), Od. 18.161, 330, Od. 19.71, Od. 20.59, Od. 21.87, 218, Od. 24.90, etc. In reference to animals Il. 10.492 (horses), Il. 11.555 = Il. 17.664 (a lion): Od. 10.217 (dogs). One's good will or favour (cf. ἀποθύμιος): ἀπὸ θυμοῦ μᾶλλον ἐμοὶ ἔσεαι Il. 1.562, σοὶ ἐκ θυμοῦ πεσέειν Il. 23.595. 7 Of the faculty of perception or knowledge: ᾔδεε κατὰ θυμὸν ὡς . . . Il. 2.409. Cf. Il. 4.163 = Il. 6.447, Il. 7.44, Il. 12.228, Il. 16.119, Il. 18.224 (of horses), Il. 20.264: οὐδὲ θυμῷ ὠΐσθη δόλον εἶναι Od. 4.452. Cf. Od. 2.112, Od. 4.730, Od. 10.374, Od. 13.339, Od. 15.211, Od. 18.154, 228, Od. 19.485 = Od. 23.260, Od. 22.373, Od. 24.391. 8 Of the faculty of thinking, deliberating, judging, considering, devising, conjecturing: ταῦθʼ ὥρμαινε κατὰ φρένα καὶ κατὰ θυμόν Il. 1.193 = Il. 11.411 = Il. 17.106 = Il. 18.15, ἥδε οἱ κατὰ θυμὸν ἀρίστη φαίνετο βουλή Il. 2.5 = Il. 10.17 = Il. 14.161, κακὰ μήσατο θυμῷ Il. 6.157, οὔ ποτε ἔλπετο θυμῷ . . . Il. 17.404. Cf. Il. 2.36, Il. 4.309, Il. 5.671, Il. 8.169, 430, Il. 9.101, 459, 537, Il. 10.447, 491, Il. 11.340, 403 = Il. 17.90 = Il. 18.5 = Il. 20.343 = Il. 21.53 = 552 = Il. 22.98, Il. 11.407 = Il. 17.97 = Il. 21.562 = Il. 22.122 = 385, Il. 13.8, Il. 14.253, Il. 15.163, 566, Il. 16.646, Il. 17.200, 442, 603, Il. 18.4, Il. 20.195, Il. 21.137, Il. 23.313, Il. 24.680: μῦθον ἔνθετο θυμῷ (laid it to heart) Od. 1.361 = Od. 21.355, ἕτερός με θ. ἔρυκεν (as if a second inward voice admonished him) Od. 9.302, νόον σχέθε τόνδʼ ἐνὶ θυμῷ Od. 14.490. Cf. Od. 1.200, 294, Od. 2.116, 156, Od. 3.128, Od. 4.117 = Od. 24.235, Od. 4.120 = Od. 5.365 = 424, Od. 5.285 = 376, Od. 5.298 = 355 = 407 = 464, Od. 6.118, Od. 9.213, 295, 299, 318 = 424 = Od. 11.230, Od. 10.50, 151, 317, 415, Od. 12.58, 217, Od. 13.154, Od. 14.150, 219, 391, Od. 15.27, 172, 202, Od. 16.73, 237, Od. 17.595, Od. 19.283, 312, 390, 524, Od. 20.5, 10, 38, 93, 217, 304 (app., you did well in not hitting . . .), Od. 22.11, Od. 23.72, 223, 345. 9 Of memory or recollection: μνήσατο κατὰ θυμὸν Αἰγίσθοιο (Ἀντιλόχοιο) Od. 1.29, Od. 4.187, ἔπος μοι ἔμπεσε θυμῷ (came into my mind) Od. 12.266. 10 Of one's character or disposition: ὥς τοι θ. ἤπια δήνεα οἶδεν Il. 4.360, οἶος κείνου θ. ὑπερφίαλος Il. 15.94. Cf. Il. 18.262, etc.: ἐμὸν θυμὸν γνώσεαι (what manner of man I am) Od. 16.309. Cf. Od. 5.191, Od. 9.272 = 368, Od. 9.287, Od. 15.20, 212, Od. 19.364, Od. 23.97, etc. II Vaguely as the seat of κῆρ 2.g: ἐμὸν κῆρ ἄχνυται ἐν θυμῷ Il. 6.524. III One's inward self as a region in which something takes place without outward manifestation: εὔχεθʼ ὃν κατὰ θυμόν (in to himself) Il. 23.769: θυμῷ ἐλέαιρε γυναῖκα (without letting any outward sign appear) Od. 19.210. Cf. Od. 5.444, Od. 20.301, Od. 22.411. IV In a more or less physical sense: ὃν θυμὸν κατέδων Il. 6.202. Cf. Il. 7.216, Il. 13.280, Il. 15.280, Il. 23.370: οὐκέτι κεύθετε θυμῷ βρωτύν Od. 18.406. Cf. Od. 9.75 = Od. 10.143, Od. 10.379.

qrh=nus.head: θρῆνυς
qrh=nus.html: θρῆνυς ὁ. 1 A foot-stool Il. 14.240, Il. 18.390: = Od. 10.315 = 367, Od. 1.131, Od. 4.136, Od. 17.409, 462, 504, Od. 19.57. 2 Prob. a plank or gangway connecting the forward and after ἴκρια of a ship: ἀνεχάζετο θρῆνυν ἐφʼ ἑπταπόδην, λίπε δʼ ἴκρια Il. 15.729.

qespe/sios.head: θεσπέσιος
qespe/sios.html: θεσπέσιος -η, -ον [θε-, θεός + σ(ε)π-. See ἐννέπω.] 1 Absol. in fem., sentence pronounced by a god, the will of heaven: εἰ καὶ θεσπεσίῃ πόλιν οὐκ ἀλαπάξεις Il. 2.367. 2 Of song, befitting a god, divinely sweet Il. 2.600. Of singers, heavenly sweet of voice: σειρήνων Od. 12.158. 3 a Of shouting or lamentation, such as might come from a god's throat, immense, deafening: ἠχῇ Il. 8.159 = Il. 15.590, Il. 12.252, Il. 13.834, Il. 15.355. Cf. Il. 16.295, Il. 18.149: βοή Od. 24.49. Cf. Od. 3.150, Od. 11.43, 633. b Of inarticulate sounds. Of the sound of branches of trees smiting each other Il. 16.769. Of that of rushing winds Il. 13.797, Il. 23.213. 4 The force of the second element lost a Of or pertaining to the gods, divine: βηλοῦ Il. 1.591. b Indicating a high degree of some quality such as abundance, greatness, greatness of extent, completeness, swiftness, beauty, sweetness or the like: πλοῦτον Il. 2.670. Cf. Il. 2.457, Il. 9.2, Il. 15.669, Il. 17.118, Il. 20.342: ὀδμή Od. 9.211. Cf. Od. 2.12 = Od. 17.63, Od. 7.42, Od. 8.19, Od. 9.68 = Od. 12.314, Od. 9.434, Od. 13.363, Od. 20.289, Od. 24.6.

qh/gw.head: θήγω
qh/gw.html: θήγω 3 sing. aor. imp. mid. θηξάσθω Il. 2.382. 1 To sharpen, whet. In mid.: δόρυ Il. 2.382. 2 Of a boar whetting his tusks Il. 11.416, Il. 13.475.

qeo/dmhtos.head: θεόδμητος
qeo/dmhtos.html: θεόδμητος [θεός + δμη-, δέμω.] God - built: πύργων Il. 8.519 (cf. Il. 21.526 cited under θεῖος 4).

qa/llw.head: †θάλλω
qa/llw.html: †θάλλω Pf. pple. τεθηλώς Od. 12.103. Fem. τεθαλυῖα, -ης Il. 9.208: Od. 6.293, Od. 11.192, 415, Od. 13.245, 410. 3 sing. plupf. τεθήλει Od. 5.69. 1 Of vegetation, to grow profusely, flourish, be luxuriant: ἡμερὶς τεθήλει σταφυλῇσιν (flourished with its. . .) Od. 5.69. 2 In pf. pple. a Growing profusely, flourishing, luxuriant: ἐρινεὸς φύλλοισι τεθηλώς Od. 12.103. Sim. of a garden, etc.: τέμενος τεθαλυῖά τʼ ἀλωή Od. 6.293. Of autumn (the season of mellow fruitfulness) Od. 11.192. b Of the fat or lard of swine, rich Od. 13.410. Sim.: συὸς ῥάχιν τεθαλυῖαν ἀλοιφῇ (rich with . . .) Il. 9.208. c Of dew, copious Od. 13.245. d Of a feast, sumptuous, affording good cheer Od. 11.415.

qra/sos.head: θράσος
qra/sos.html: θράσος τό [=θάρσος.] Boldness, courage: οὐκ ἔχει θράσος ὅς κεν ἴδηται Il. 14.416.

qhri/on.head: θηρίον
qhri/on.html: θηρίον τό [prob. θήρ + suffix distinguishing an individual from a class.] A wild beast: μάλα μέγα θηρίον ἦεν Od. 10.171, 180.

qaa/ssw.head: θαάσσω
qaa/ssw.html: θαάσσω [cf. θῶκος.] To sit, be seated: ἕδος ἔνθα θάασσεν Il. 9.194. Cf. Il. 15.124: δηθὰ θεῶν ἐν δαιτὶ θαασσέμεν Od. 3.336.

qru/on.head: θρύον
qru/on.html:
θρύον τό. Collectively, rushes Il. 21.351.
Θρύον (Ἀλφειοῖο πόρος). A town of Pylus Il. 2.592 , apparently identical with Θρυόεσσα (αἰπεῖα κολώνη) Il. 11.711 .

qale/qw.head: θαλέθω
qale/qw.html: θαλέθω [θάλλω.] In pres. pple., flourishing, luxuriant: θάμνος ἐλαίης Od. 23.191. Of youths, lusty, in prime of vigour Od. 6.63. Of swine: θαλέθοντες ἀλοιφῇ (swelling with fat) Il. 9.467, Il. 23.32.

qeoprope/w.head: θεοπροπέω
qeoprope/w.html: θεοπροπέω [θεοπρόπος.] To reveal the divine will Il. 1.109, Il. 2.322: Od. 2.184.

qau=ma.head: θαῦμα
qau=ma.html: θαῦμα τό [θαϝ- as in θάομαι1.] 1 Wonder, amazement: θ. μʼ ἔχει Od. 10.326. 2 A wonder or marvel: θ. ἰδέσθαι (to behold) Il. 5.725, Il. 10.439, Il. 18.83, 377, μέγα θ. τόδʼ ὁρῶμαι (this is a great wonder that I see) Il. 13.99 = Il. 15.286 = Il. 20.344 = Il. 21.54. Cf. Il. 18.549: Od. 6.306, Od. 7.45, Od. 8.366, Od. 9.190, Od. 11.287, Od. 13.108, Od. 17.306, Od. 19.36.

qh/bh.head: Θήβη-1.
qh/bh.html:
Θήβη-1. See Θῆβαι-1.
Θήβη-2 Θῆβαι-3 Il. 22.479 (ἱερή, ὑποπλακίη, ὑψίπυλος). A town (inhabited by the Cilices), of which Eetion-1 was king, in the plain of Thebe-2 in which Adramyttium afterwards stood. Taken by Achilles and Eetion-1 slain and Chryseis captured Il. 1.366, Il. 2.691, Il. 6.397, 416; Il. 22.479 .

qrasuka/rdios.head: θρασυκάρδιος
qrasuka/rdios.html: θρασυκάρδιος [θρασύς + καρδίη.] Stout of heart Il. 10.41, Il. 13.343.

qersi/ths.head: Θερσίτης
qersi/ths.html: Θερσίτης A deformed Greek described Il. 2.212. Abuses Agamemnon Il. 2.225, Odysseus deals with him 244, 246.

qarse/w.head: θαρσέω
qarse/w.html: θαρσέω [θάρσος.] 3 pl. pf. τεθαρσήκασι Il. 9.420, 687. 1 To be of good heart or courage, of good cheer: θαρσῶν μάχεσθαι Il. 5.124, τεθαρσήκασι λαοί (are (now) of good heart) Il. 9.420 = 687. In imp. θάρσει Il. 4.184, Il. 8.39 = Il. 22.183, Il. 10.383, Il. 15.254, Il. 18.463, Il. 24.171: Od. 2.372, Od. 4.825, Od. 8.197 (τόνδε γʼ ἄεθλον, as touching this . . .), Od. 13.362 = Od. 16.436 = Od. 24.357, Od. 19.546, Od. 22.372. 2 In aor., to take heart, pluck up courage: θαρσήσας εἰπέ Il. 1.85. Cf. Il. 1.92, Il. 20.338: Od. 3.76, 252.

qhteu/w.head: θητεύω
qhteu/w.html: θητεύω [θητ-, θής.] To serve as a hired labourer: θητεύσαμεν μισθῷ ἔπι ῥητῷ Il. 21.444. Cf. Od. 11.489, Od. 18.357.

qrasumh/dhs.head: Θρασυμήδης
qrasumh/dhs.html: Θρασυμήδης (ἀντίθεος, δῖος, ἱππόδαμος, κυδάλιμος, μενεπτόλεμος, ποιμὴν λαῶν , ὑπέρθυμος). Patronymic Νεστορίδης. Son of Nestor Il. 9.81 , Il. 10.255, Il. 14.10; slays Maris Il. 16.321 ; Il. 17.378, 705: Od. 3.39, 414, 442, 448.

qrw/|skw.head: θρῴσκω
qrw/|skw.html: θρῴσκω 3 sing. aor. ἔθορε Il. 4.79, Il. 7.182, Il. 15.573: Od. 10.207. θόρε Il. 8.320, Il. 15.582, Il. 20.381, Il. 23.353, 509. 3 pl. θόρον Il. 8.252, Il. 14.441, Il. 15.380. 3 pl. subj. θόρωσι Od. 22.303. Pple. θορών, -όντος Il. 5.161, Il. 10.528, Il. 11.70, Il. 15.580, Il. 16.770, 773. Fem. θοροῦσα Od. 23.32. (ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, ἐσ-, προ-, ὑπερ-.) To leap, spring, bound, dart: κὰδ δʼ ἔθορʼ ἐς μέσσον Il. 4.79. Cf. Il. 5.161, Il. 8.252 = Il. 14.441, Il. 8.320 = Il. 23.509, Il. 10.528, Il. 11.70 = Il. 17.770, Il. 15.380, 573, 580, 582, 684, Il. 20.381, Il. 21.126: ἀπὸ λέκτροιο θοροῦσα Od. 23.32. Cf. Od. 22.303. Of inanimate objects: ἐκ δʼ ἔθορε κλῆρος κυνέης Il. 7.182. Cf. Il. 13.589, Il. 15.314, 470, Il. 16.773, Il. 23.353: Od. 10.207.

qarsu/nw.head: θαρσύνω
qarsu/nw.html: θαρσύνω [θάρσος.] 3 sing. pa. iterative θαρσύνεσκε Il. 4.233. 2 sing. aor. θάρσυνας Od. 13.323. 3 sing. -ε Il. 10.190. Subj. θαρσύνω Od. 3.361. Imp. θάρσυνον Il. 16.242. (ἐπι-.) To encourage, hearten, cheer, put spirit into: τοὺς θάρσυνε μύθῳ Il. 10.190. Cf. Il. 4.233, Il. 13.767 = Il. 17.117 = 683, Il. 16.242, Il. 18.325, Il. 23.682: Od. 3.361, Od. 9.377, Od. 13.323, Od. 16.448, Od. 24.448.

qermo/s.head: θερμός
qermo/s.html: θερμός [θέρω.] Warm, hot: λοετρά Il. 14.6, Il. 22.444. Cf. Il. 7.426, Il. 11.266, Il. 16.3, Il. 17.438, Il. 18.17, 235: Od. 4.523, Od. 8.249, 451, Od. 9.388, Od. 14.77, Od. 19.362, 388, Od. 24.46.

qa/mbos.head: θάμβος
qa/mbos.html: θάμβος τό. Genit. θάμβευς Od. 24.394. Wonder, astonishment, amazement: θ. ἔχεν εἰσορόωντας Il. 3.342. Cf. Il. 4.79, Il. 23.815, Il. 24.482: Od. 3.372, Od. 24.394.

quh/eis.head: θυήεις
quh/eis.html: θυήεις [θύος. Cf. θυόεις.] Fragrant with the savour of sacrifice: βωμός Il. 8.48, Il. 23.148: Od. 8.363.

qu/sanos.head: θύσανος
qu/sanos.html: θύσανος -ου, ὁ. A tassel or pendant. Attached to the aegis: παγχρύσεοι ἐϋπλεκέες Il. 2.448 (app. of twisted wire). To Here's girdle Il. 14.181.

qa/natos.head: θάνατος
qa/natos.html:
θάνατος -ου, ὁ [θαν-, θνῄσκω.] 1 Death Il. 1.60, Il. 2.302, Il. 3.101, Il. 5.68, Il. 9.571, etc.: Od. 2.100, Od. 3.236, Od. 4.180, Od. 9.467, Od. 11.488, etc. 2 Personified: Ὕπνῳ κασιγνήτῳ Θανάτοιο Il. 14.231. Cf. Il. 16.454, 672 = 682. 3 A kind or mode of death: λευγαλέῳ θανάτῳ ἁλῶναι Il. 21.281: = Od. 5.312, πάντες στυγεροὶ θάνατοί [εἰσιν] Od. 12.341. Cf. Od. 11.412, Od. 15.359, Od. 18.202, Od. 22.462, Od. 24.34.
Θάνατος See Lexicon.

qa/leia.head: Θάλεια
qa/leia.html: Θάλεια A Nereid Il. 18.39 .

qe/skelos.head: θέσκελος
qe/skelos.html: θέσκελος [the first element seems to be the same as in θέσ-φατος.] 1 App., marvellous, wondrous, or the like: ἔργα Il. 3.130: Od. 11.374, 610.– 2 So in neut. θέσκελον as adv., marvellously, in wondrous wise: ἔϊκτο θέσκελον αὐτῷ Il. 23.107.

qhreuth/s.head: θηρευτής
qhreuth/s.html: θηρευτής ὁ [θηρεύω.] A hunter Il. 12.41. With κύων, a hunting dog: ἐν κυσὶ θηρευτῇσιν Il. 11.325.

qu/w.head: θύω1
qu/w.html:
θύω1 [cf. θύνω.] 1 To run, rush: ἔγχεϊ (spear in hand) Il. 11.180, Il. 16.699, Il. 22.272. Of a river Il. 21.234, 324. Of the sea Il. 23.230: Od. 13.85. Of the wind Od. 12.400, 408, 426 Fig.: ὀλοιῇσι φρεσὶ θύει Il. 1.342. 2 To run or flow (with a liquid): δάπεδον ἅπαν αἵματι θῦεν Od. 11.420, Od. 22.309 = Od. 24.185.
θύω2. 1 To offer in sacrifice portions of a meal before partaking: θεοῖσι θῦσαι ἀνώγει Il. 9.219. Cf. Od. 9.231, Od. 15.222, 260. 2 To offer (such portions to the gods): ἄργματα θῦσε θεοῖς Od. 14.446.

qe/mis.head: θέμις
qe/mis.html:
θέμις -ιστος, ἡ [θε-, τίθημι]. 1 In pl., a body of traditionary rules or precedents: βασιλεύς, ᾧ δῶκε κρόνου πάϊς θέμιστας Il. 2.206. Cf. Il. 1.238, Il. 9.99: Od. 9.112, 215 (see δίκη 2). In sing.: ὃς οὔ τινα οἶδε θέμιστα Il. 5.761 (has no regard for any usage of decency; see εἴδω III.12). 2 What is established or sanctioned by custom or usage: ἣ θ. ἐστίν Il. 2.73 (as is my right), Il. 9.33 (do.), Il. 23.581 (as usage requires), Il. 24.652 (as the custom is), ἣ θ. ἀνθρώπων πέλει (as is the way of . . .) Il. 9.134, ἣ θ. ἐστὶν ἤ τʼ ἀνδρῶν ἤ τε γυναικῶν (as is the way of . . .) 276 = Il. 19.177, ξείνια παρέθηκεν, ἅ τε ξείνοις θ. ἐστίν (which by the customs of hospitality one . . .) Il. 11.779, ἄορ ἔχων: τῷ δʼ οὐ θ. ἐστὶ μιγῆναι (mortal must not encounter it) Il. 14.386, πάρος γʼ οὐ θ. ἦεν . . . (it was not permitted . . .) Il. 16.796, οὐ θ. ἐστὶ . . . (it must not be that . . .) Il. 23.44: ἣ θ. ἐστίν Od. 3.45 (as the custom is), 187 (as is your due), Od. 11.451 (as it is his privilege to do), ἥ τε ξείνων θ. ἐστίν (as . . . use to do) Od. 9.268, οὔ μοι θ. ἐστὶ . . . (I may not . . .) Od. 10.73, Od. 14.56, ἣ θ. ἐστὶ γυναικός (as a woman's way ever is) 130, ἐπεί μοι . . . θ. ἐστίν (since it is my right to . . .) Od. 16.91, ἡ γὰρ θ. ὅς τις . . . (for that is due to him who . . .) Od. 24.286. 3 A judgment or doom Il. 16.387. 4 An ordinance or decree Il. 9.156, 298. 5 An oracular reply (in answer to an inquiry as to what is right to be done) Od. 16.403. 6 A place of judgment Il. 11.807. 7 As proper name, a goddess with such funtions as may be gathered from the name and the context Il. 15.87, 93, Il. 20.4: Od. 2.68.
Θέμις See θέμις 7 in Lexicon.

qa/los.head: θάλος
qa/los.html: θάλος τό [θάλλω.] A young shoot or branch. Fig. of a youthful person Il. 22.87: Od. 6.157.

qou=ros.head: θοῦρος
qou=ros.html: θοῦρος and in fem. form θοῦρις, -ιδος, with acc. -ιν [θορ-, θρῴσκω.] Rushing, impetuous, eager for the fray. Epithet 1 Of Ares Il. 5.30, 35, 355, 454, 507, 830, 904, Il. 15.127, 142, Il. 21.406, Il. 24.498. 2 Of ἀλκή Il. 4.234, Il. 6.112, Il. 7.164, Il. 11.313, Il. 18.157, etc.: Od. 4.527. 3 Of a shield, app. by transference of epithet from the bearer to the shield: ἀσπίδα θοῦριν Il. 11.32, Il. 20.162. Sim. of the aegis Il. 15.308.

qnh/|skw.head: θνῄσκω
qnh/|skw.html: θνῄσκω Fut. infin. in mid. form θανέεσθαι Il. 4.12, Il. 15.728: Od. 20.21. Aor. θάνον Od. 11.412. 2 sing. θάνες Il. 22.486: Od. 24.37. 3 sing. ἔθανε Il. 21.610: Od. 3.248, Od. 8.226. θάνε Il. 2.642: Od. 1.396, Od. 2.96, Od. 15.253, Od. 19.141, Od. 24.131. 3 pl. θάνον Il. 12.13: Od. 9.66, Od. 11.389, Od. 24.22. Subj. θάνω Il. 11.455, Il. 18.121. 2 sing. θάνῃς Il. 4.170, Il. 22.55. 3 sing. θάνῃσι Il. 19.228: Od. 4.196, Od. 11.218. 1 pl. θάνωμεν Od. 12.156. 3 pl. θάνωσι Il. 7.410. 3 sing. opt. θάνοι Od. 15.359. 3 pl. θάνοιεν Od. 22.472. Imp. θάνε Il. 21.106. Pple. θανών, -όντος Il. 7.80, Il. 8.476, Il. 11.453, Il. 15.350, Il. 16.457, 675, Il. 17.120, 182, 379, 538, 564, Il. 18.195, Il. 21.28, Il. 22.73, 343, 389, Il. 23.9, 70, 223, Il. 24.16, 575: Od. 1.236, Od. 3.258, Od. 4.553, Od. 5.310, Od. 11.486, 554, Od. 17.115, 312, Od. 24.77, 79, 93, 190, 296, 436. Infin. θανέειν Il. 15.289, Il. 22.426: Od. 1.59, Od. 4.562, Od. 5.308, Od. 12.342, Od. 14.274. θανεῖν Il. 7.52. 3 sing. pf. τέθνηκε Il. 18.12: Od. 1.196, Od. 2.132, Od. 4.110, 199, 834, 837, Od. 11.461, 464, Od. 20.208, Od. 24.264. 3 pl. τεθνᾶσι Il. 7.328, Il. 22.52: Od. 11.304, Od. 15.350. Opt. τεθναίην Il. 18.98. 2 sing. τεθναίης Il. 6.164. 3 sing. τεθναίη Il. 3.102. Imp. τέθναθι Il. 22.365. 3 sing. τεθνάτω Il. 15.496. Pple. τεθνηώς Il. 17.161. Genit. τεθνηῶτος Il. 9.633, Il. 13.659, Il. 18.173, Il. 19.210, Il. 23.192, Il. 24.244: Od. 1.289, Od. 2.220. τεθνηότος Il. 17.435: Od. 15.23, Od. 24.56. Dat. τεθνηῶτι Od. 10.494. τεθνεῶτι Od. 19.331. Acc. τεθνηῶτα Il. 6.464, Il. 16.858, Il. 17.229, 341, Il. 18.537, Il. 19.289, 403, Il. 22.364: Od. 12.10. τεθνηότα Il. 17.402, Il. 19.300, Il. 24.20. Genit. pl. τεθνηώτων Il. 16.16. Acc. τεθνηῶτας Il. 6.71. τεθνηότας Od. 23.84. Acc. sing. fem. τεθνηυῖαν Od. 4.734. Infin. τεθνάμεναι Il. 24.225. τεθνάμεν Il. 15.497, Il. 17.405, Il. 19.335: Od. 16.107, Od. 20.317, Od. 21.155. (ἀπο-, ἐκ-, κατα-.) 1 To die: θνῄσκων ἔλιπε Θυέστῃ Il. 2.106. Cf. Il. 1.56, 383, Il. 4.12, 170, Il. 7.52, 410, Il. 11.455, Il. 15.728, Il. 18.121, Il. 19.228, Il. 21.106, Il. 22.55, Il. 24.743: θανέειν ἱμείρεται Od. 1.59. Cf. Od. 4.196, 562, Od. 5.308, Od. 8.526, Od. 11.218, Od. 12.22, 156, 342, Od. 14.274, Od. 15.359, Od. 20.21, Od. 22.472. 2 In a quasi- passive sense of being slain in battle: χερσὶν ὑπʼ Αἴαντος θανέειν Il. 15.289. Cf. Il. 1.243, Il. 22.426. 3 In aor. indic. a In strict aor. sense: αἶψʼ ἔθανεν Εὔρυτος Od. 8.226. Cf. Od. 3.248, Od. 9.66, Od. 11.389 = Od. 24.22, Od. 11.412, Od. 24.37. In pple.: ἀνδρὸς τῆλε θανόντος (that met his death . . .) Od. 17.312, θανὼν φθιμένοισι μετείην (may I die and . . .) Od. 24.436. b To have died, be dead: θάνε Μελέαγρος Il. 2.642. Cf. Il. 12.13, Il. 21.610, Il. 22.486: ἐπεὶ θάνʼ Ὀδυσσεύς Od. 1.396, Od. 2.96 = Od. 19.141 = Od. 24.131. Cf. Od. 15.253. In pple.: ὄφρα πυρός με λελάχωσι θανόντα (in death) Il. 7.80 = Il. 22.343, περὶ πατρόκλοιο θανόντος (the dead . . .) Il. 8.476, Il. 17.120, 182, Il. 18.195, μενοιτιάδαο θανόντος ἄχεος (for the death of . . .) Il. 17.538, οὔ μευ ζώοντος . . ., ἀλλὰ θανόντος (now that I am dead) Il. 23.70. Cf. Il. 11.453, Il. 15.350, Il. 17.379, 564, Il. 21.28, Il. 22.73, Il. 23.223, Il. 24.16, 575: οὔ κε θανόντι περ ὧδʼ ἀκαχοίμην (if he were dead) Od. 1.236, ζωὸς ἠὲ θανών (alive or dead) Od. 4.553, μή τι θανὼν ἀκαχίζευ (let not thy death grieve thee) Od. 11.486. Cf. Od. 3.258, Od. 5.310, Od. 11.554, Od. 17.115, Od. 24.77, 79, 93. Absol. in pl. pple., the dead: γέρας θανόντων Il. 16.457 = 675, Il. 23.9: Od. 24.190, 296. Cf. Il. 22.389. 4 In pf. a To be dead: τεθναίη (let him lie dead) Il. 3.102, πολλοὶ τεθνᾶσιν Il. 7.328, οὔ ποτε ἔλπετο τεθνάμεν (that the was dead) Il. 17.405. Cf. Il. 6.164, Il. 15.496, 497, Il. 18.12, 98, Il. 19.335, Il. 22.52, 365, Il. 24.225: ζώει ὅ γʼ ἦ τέθνηκεν Od. 2.132, Od. 4.110, 837 = Od. 11.464. Cf. Od. 4.199, 834 = Od. 24.264, Od. 11.304, Od. 15.350, Od. 16.107, Od. 20.208, 317, Od. 21.155. In pple., dead: νεκροὺς τεθνηῶτας (the dead bodies) Il. 6.71. Cf. Il. 6.464, Il. 9.633, Il. 13.659, Il. 16.16, 858, Il. 17.161, 229, 341, 402, 435, Il. 18.173, 537, Il. 19.210, 289, 300, 403, Il. 22.364, Il. 23.192, Il. 24.20, 244: εἴ κε τεθνηῶτος ἀκούσῃς (hear of his death) Od. 1.289. Cf. Od. 2.220, Od. 4.734, Od. 10.494, Od. 12.10, Od. 15.23, Od. 19.331, Od. 23.84, Od. 24.56. b In strict pf. sense: οὔ πω τέθνηκεν Ὀδυσσεύς (Ὀρέστης) Od. 1.196, Od. 11.461.

qhseu/s.head: Θησεύς
qhseu/s.html: Θησεύς (ἐπιείκελος ἀθανάτοισιν, ἐρικυδής). Patronymic Αἰγεΐδης. Son of Aegeus, king of Athens, and husband of Phaedra. The great legendary hero of Athens. Named as a warrior of Nestor's youth Il. 1.265: carried off Ariadne from Crete Od. 11.322; Od. 11.631.

qurawro/s.head: θυραωρός
qurawro/s.html: θυραωρός [θύρη + ὀρ-, ὄρομαι.] Watching the door, watch(-dogs): κύνας θυραωρούς Il. 22.69.

qa/rsos.head: θάρσος
qa/rsos.html: θάρσος τό [θράσος.] Genit. θάρσευς Il. 17.573. 1 Boldness, courage, spirit, confidence: σῷ θάρσει Il. 6.126. Cf. Il. 5.2, Il. 7.153, Il. 17.570, 573, Il. 21.547: Od. 1.321, Od. 3.76, Od. 6.140, Od. 9.381, Od. 14.216. 2 Excessive boldness or confidence: θ. ἄητον ἔχουσα Il. 21.395.

qe/rmw.head: †θέρμω
qe/rmw.html: †θέρμω [θέρω.] 2 pl. aor. imp. θέρμετε Od. 8.426. 3 sing. aor. mid. θέρμετο Il. 18.348, Il. 23.381: Od. 8.437. 1 To warm, heat: ὕδωρ Od. 8.426. 2 In mid., to become warm or hot: θέρμετο δʼ ὕδωρ Il. 18.348: = Od. 8.437. Cf. Il. 23.381.

qeanw/.head: Θεανώ
qeanw/.html: Θεανώ (δῖα, καλλιπάρῃος ). Patronymic Κισσηΐς. Daughter of Cisses (Il. 11.224), wife of Antenor, mother of Iphidamas and priestess at Troy of Athene . Brought up Pedaeus Il. 5.70; opens Athene's temple for the aged women Il. 6.298, 302.

qa/sswn.head: θάσσων
qa/sswn.html: θάσσων -ονος [for θακίων. Comp. of ταχύς with transference of aspirate.] 1 Swifter: ποσὶν θ. (with the feet, in running) Il. 15.570. Cf. Il. 13.819. 2 In neut. θᾶσσον as adv. a The quicker, the speedier, the sooner: ὄφρα κε θ. ἐγείρομεν Ἄρηα Il. 2.440. Cf. Il. 6.143 = Il. 20.429, Il. 12.26, Il. 23.53: Od. 2.307, Od. 10.33. b Quickly rather than slowly, quickly, with speed: θ. Ἀθηναίῃ ἐπιτεῖλαι Il. 4.64. Cf. Il. 13.115, Il. 16.129, Il. 17.654, Il. 19.68, Il. 20.257: ἔρρʼ ἐκ νήσου θ. Od. 10.72. Cf. Od. 7.152, Od. 10.44, 192, 228, 268, Od. 15.201, Od. 16.130, Od. 20.154, Od. 24.495.

qa/ptw.head: θάπτω
qa/ptw.html: θάπτω 3 pl. aor. θάψαν Il. 24.612. 3 sing. plupf. pass. ἐτέθαπτο Od. 11.52. (κατα-.) To pay funeral rites to (a corpse): ὁπότʼ Ἀμαρυγκέα θάπτον Ἐπειοί Il. 23.630. Cf. Il. 21.323, Il. 23.71, Il. 24.612, 665: οὔ πω ἐτέθαπτο Od. 11.52. Cf. Od. 3.285, Od. 12.12, Od. 24.417.

qambe/w.head: θαμβέω
qambe/w.html: θαμβέω [θάμβος.] 1 To wonder, be struck with wonder or astonishment: θάμβησεν Ἀχιλεύς Il. 1.199. Cf. Il. 3.398, Il. 8.77, Il. 23.728 = 881, Il. 24.483, 484: θαμβήσασα βεβήκει Od. 1.360 = Od. 21.354. Cf. Od. 1.323, Od. 4.638, Od. 10.63, Od. 24.101. 2 To wonder or marvel at: ὄρνιθας Od. 2.155. Cf. Od. 16.178, Od. 17.367.

qh/r.head: θήρ
qh/r.html: θήρ θηρός, ὁ. Dat. pl. θήρεσσι Od. 5.473, Od. 14.21. θηρσί Od. 24.292. A wild beast, wild creature Il. 3.449, Il. 8.47, Il. 10.184, Il. 11.119, 546, Il. 14.283, Il. 15.151, 324, 586, 633, Il. 21.470, 485: Od. 5.473, Od. 11.573, Od. 14.21, Od. 24.292.

qu/sqla.head: θύσθλα
qu/sqla.html: θύσθλα τά. App., mystic implements borne in the rites of Dionysus: θ. χαμαὶ κατέχευαν Il. 6.134.

qrh=nos.head: θρῆνος
qrh=nos.html: θρῆνος ὁ [cf. θρόος.] A funeral-song, a dirge: θρήνων ἐξάρχους Il. 24.721.

qumobo/ros.head: θυμοβόρος
qumobo/ros.html: θυμοβόρος -ον [θυμός + βορ-, βι-βρώσκω.] Eating the heart, that will not leave the heart in peace. Epithet of ἔρις Il. 7.210, 301, Il. 16.476, Il. 19.58, Il. 20.253.

qw/s.head: θώς
qw/s.html: θώς Genit. pl. θώων Il. 13.103. A beast of prey, perh. the jackal Il. 11.474, 479, 481, Il. 13.103.

qro/os.head: θρόος
qro/os.html: θρόος ὁ. Sound, noise; hence, speech Il. 4.437.

qwrh/ssw.head: θωρήσσω
qwrh/ssw.html: θωρήσσω [θώρηξ.] 3 sing. aor. θώρηξε Il. 16.155. 1 pl. subj. θωρήξομεν Il. 2.72, 83. Infin. θωρῆξαι Il. 2.11, 28, 65. Fut. mid. θωρήξομαι Il. 7.101, Il. 19.23. Aor. subj. θωρήξομαι Il. 8.376. 3 pl. aor. pass. θωρήχθησαν Il. 3.340, Il. 23.813. Nom. pl. masc. pple. θωρηχθέντες Il. 8.530, Il. 11.49, 725, Il. 12.77, Il. 13.699, Il. 16.257, Il. 18.277, 303. Infin. θωρηχθῆναι Il. 1.226, Il. 16.40: Od. 22.139. (ὑπο-.) 1 In act., to cause to arm for the fray, get under arms: Ἀχαιούς Il. 2.11, 28 = 65. Cf. Il. 2.72 = 83, Il. 16.155. 2 In mid. and pass. a to arm oneself for the fray, get under arms, don one's harness: τῷδε θωρήξομαι (to meet him) Il. 7.101, δός μοι τὰ σὰ τεύχεα θωρηχθῆναι (to arm myself withal) Il. 16.40. Cf. Il. 1.226, Il. 3.340, Il. 8.54, Il. 11.715, Il. 18.189, etc.: Od. 12.227, Od. 22.139, Od. 23.369. b App. meaning little more than to have one's station, post oneself, stand, be: ἐπʼ ἀριστερὰ θωρήσσοντο Il. 2.526, πρὸ φθίων θωρηχθέντες (acting as their leaders) Il. 13.699, ἅμα πατρόκλῳ θωρηχθέντες (following him) Il. 16.257. Cf. Il. 2.587, 818, Il. 4.252, Il. 11.709, Il. 16.218.

quosko/os.head: θυοσκόος
quosko/os.html: θυοσκόος -ου, ὁ [θυ-, θύος + σκο- as in σκοπός.] App. a religious adviser skilled in divination from sacrifices, perh. from observation of the smoke thereof Od. 21.145, Od. 22.318, 321. Joined with μάντις Il. 24.221.

quga/thr.head: θυγάτηρ
quga/thr.html: θυγάτηρ ἡ [cognate with Eng. daughter, German tochter.] Genit. θυγατέρος Il. 21.504: Od. 19.400. θυγατρός Od. 4.4, Od. 7.290, Od. 11.421. Dat. θυγατέρι Od. 10.106, Od. 15.364. θυγατρί Il. 9.148, 290. Acc. θυγατέρα Il. 5.371, Il. 6.192, Il. 11.626, Il. 21.88, etc. θύγατρα Il. 1.13, 95, 372, Il. 11.740: Od. 2.53, Od. 11.260, 269, Od. 18.276. Voc. θύγατερ Il. 5.348, Il. 7.24, Il. 14.194, etc.: Od. 1.10, Od. 8.464, Od. 20.61, etc. Nom. pl. θυγατέρες Il. 2.492, Il. 11.271, Il. 24.166, 604: Od. 3.451, Od. 10.6. θύγατρες Il. 6.238, Il. 9.144, 286, Il. 22.155: Od. 11.227. Genit. θυγατρῶν Il. 2.715, Il. 6.252, Il. 13.365, Il. 21.142, etc.: Od. 3.452. Dat. θυγατέρεσσι Il. 15.197. Acc. θυγατέρας Od. 10.7. θύγατρας Il. 22.62: Od. 11.329, Od. 22.222. A daughter, one's daughter Il. 1.13, 538, Il. 2.548, 715, Il. 6.238, 398, etc.: Od. 1.52, Od. 2.53, Od. 3.452, 465, Od. 4.4, Od. 7.290, etc.

qeeio/w.head: θεειόω
qeeio/w.html: θεειόω [θέειον] (διαθειόω). To cleanse with the fumes of sulphur Od. 22.482. In mid. Od. 23.50.

qu/retra.head: θύρετρα
qu/retra.html: θύρετρα τά [θύρη.] A door (cf. θύρη 1..b) Il. 2.415: αὐλῆς θ. (app., a door leading to the αὐλή from the λαύρη) Od. 22.137. Cf. Od. 18.385, Od. 21.49.

qro/nos.head: θρόνος
qro/nos.html: θρόνος -ου, ὁ. A seat or chair: καθέζετʼ ἐπὶ θρόνου Il. 1.536. Cf. Il. 8.199, 442, Il. 11.645, Il. 14.238, Il. 15.124, 142, 150, Il. 18.389, 422, Il. 20.62, Il. 24.515, 522, 553: κατὰ κλισμούς τε θρόνους τε (the two words hardly to be distinguished) Od. 1.145. Cf. Od. 1.130, Od. 4.51, Od. 5.86, Od. 6.308, Od. 8.65, Od. 17.32, Od. 20.96, Od. 22.23, etc.

qami/zw.head: θαμίζω
qami/zw.html: θαμίζω [θαμά.] 1 To come often to, frequent, an indicated place: πάρος γε μὲν οὔ τι θαμίζεις Il. 18.386 = 425: Od. 5.88. 2 To go about, ply one's vocation: ἅμα νηῒ θαμίζων Od. 8.161. 3 With pass. pple., to be accustomed to treatment of an indicated kind: οὔ τι κομιζόμενος θάμιζεν (was not wont to be (so) cared for) Od. 8.451.

qalusia/dhs.head: Θαλυσιάδης
qalusia/dhs.html: Θαλυσιάδης Patronymic of Echepolus-1 Il. 4.458.

qow/ths.head: Θοώτης
qow/ths.html: Θοώτης (δῖος). A Greek herald Il. 12.342, 343 .

qhbai=os.head: Θηβαῖος-1
qhbai=os.html:
Θηβαῖος-1 (ὑπέρθυμος). Father of Eniopeus Il. 8.120.
Θηβαῖος-2. Adj. from Θῆβαι-1. Of Teiresias Od. 10.492, 565, Od. 11.90 , 165, Od. 12.267, Od. 23.323.

qame/es.head: θαμέες
qame/es.html: θαμέες Nom. pl. fem. θαμειαί. Acc. θαμειάς. 1 Set or standing closely together: ἔνθα θαμειαὶ εἴρυντο νέες Il. 18.68. Cf. Il. 10.264, Il. 12.296, Il. 19.383 = Il. 22.316: ἀραρὼν θαμέσι σταμίνεσσιν Od. 5.252. Cf. Od. 12.92, Od. 14.12. 2 coming, flying, falling, thick and fast: θαμέες ἄκοντες ἀΐσσουσιν Il. 11.552 = Il. 17.661, ὥς τε νιφάδες πίπτωσι θαμειαί Il. 12.278. Cf. Il. 12.44, 287, Il. 14.422. 3 Occurring at short intervals over a space, numerous: πυραὶ καίοντο θαμειαί Il. 1.52.

qu/raze.head: θύραζε
qu/raze.html: θύραζε [θύρη.] 1 Out through a door, out of a room or house: βῆ θ. (from his smithy) Il. 18.416. Cf. Il. 24.572: ἢν ἕλκωσι θ. Od. 16.276. Cf. Od. 6.53, Od. 15.62, 451, Od. 19.69, Od. 21.238 = 384. Of leaving a cave Od. 9.418, 444, 461. Of passing the gates of dreams Od. 19.566. With ἐκ: ἐκ θ. ἔδραμον (out of doors) Il. 18.29: δόμων ἐξῆγε θ. Od. 15.465. Cf. Od. 18.386, Od. 19.68, Od. 20.179, 361, 367, Od. 21.89, 299, 388. In pregnant sense: ἐξελθόντες μεγάρων ἕζεσθε θ. (out of doors) Od. 22.375. Cf. Od. 20.97, Od. 22.456. 2 Forth from a specified or indicated space or region: [ἰχθὺν] ἔρριψε θ. (out of the sea) Od. 12.254, διὰ δʼ ἀμπερὲς ἦλθε θ. ἰός (through and out from the axe-heads) Od. 21.422. With ἐκ: οὐδὲ θ. εἴων ἐξιέναι (from the line of the ships) Il. 18.447. Cf. Il. 5.694, Il. 16.408, Il. 21.29, 237: Od. 5.410.

qe/speia.head: Θέσπεια
qe/speia.html: Θέσπεια A Boeotian town Il. 2.498.

qu/os.head: θύος
qu/os.html: θύος τό [θύω2.] Dat. pl. θυέεσσι Il. 6.270, Il. 9.499. 1 A making of sacrifice, a sacrifice or offering Il. 9.499. In pl. of a single offering: λίσσομʼ ὑπὲρ θυέων Od. 15.261. 2 What is sacrificed or offered: πρὸς νηὸν ἔρχεο σὺν θυέεσσιν Il. 6.270.

qoo/s.head: θοός
qoo/s.html: θοός -ή, -όν [θεϝ-, θέω.] 1 Quick in movement, nimble, swift, fleet: θοός περ ἐὼν πολεμιστής Il. 5.571. Cf. Il. 5.536, Il. 12.306, Il. 15.585, Il. 16.422, 494. 2 a Epithet of Ares Il. 5.430, Il. 8.215, Il. 13.295 = 328, 528, Il. 16.784, Il. 17.72, 536. Of warriors Il. 2.542, 758, Il. 5.462. b Of ships Il. 1.12, 300, 308, Il. 2.619, Il. 9.332, Il. 12.112, etc.: Od. 1.260, 303, Od. 3.61, Od. 4.173, 255, 779, etc. c Of night (app. thought of as a body of darkness passing swiftly over the earth) Il. 10.394, 468, Il. 12.463, Il. 14.261, Il. 24.366 = 653: Od. 12.284. d Of a chariot Il. 11.533 = Il. 17.458. e Of a whip, quickly making itself felt Il. 17.430. f Of a meal, perh., deftly served Od. 8.38. g Of a missile Od. 22.83. 3 νήσοισιν ἐπιπροέηκε θοῇσιν Od. 15.299. Doubtfully explained (cf. θοόω) as the sharp or pointed islands, supposed to form part of the group called the Echinades.

qalero/s.head: θαλερός
qalero/s.html: θαλερός -ή, -όν [θάλλω.] 1 Lusty, in prime of vigour: αἰζηοί Il. 3.26. Cf. Il. 4.474, Il. 6.430, Il. 8.156, 190, Il. 10.259, Il. 14.4, etc. 2 Of a woman, blooming, in pride of beauty: παράκοιτιν Il. 3.53. 3 Of marriage, app. giving the notion of the union of a pair in prime of youth Od. 6.66, Od. 20.74. 4 Of parts of the body, well-developed, stout: μηρώ Il. 15.113. Of a horse's mane, long, flowing Il. 17.439. 5 Of the voice, full, rich Il. 17.696 = Il. 23.397: = Od. 4.705 = Od. 19.472. 6 Of tears, big Il. 2.266, Il. 6.496, Il. 24.9, 794: Od. 4.556, Od. 10.201, 409, 570, Od. 11.5, 391, 466, Od. 12.12, Od. 16.16, Od. 22.447. 7 Of lamentation, loud, vehement Od. 10.457. 8 Of fat, thick, abundant Od. 8.476.

que/sths.head: Θυέστης
que/sths.html: Θυέστης Θυέστα Il. 2.107 (πολύαρνι). Son of Pelops, brother of Atreus and father of Aegisthus. The sceptre left to him by Atreus and by him to Agamemnon Il. 2.106 , 107: his dwelling Od. 4.517 .

qumole/wn.head: θυμολέων
qumole/wn.html: θυμολέων -οντος [θυμός + λέων.] Lion-hearted: πόσιν Od. 4.724 = 814. Epithet of Heracles Il. 5.639: Od. 11.267. Of Achilles Il. 7.228.

qrhne/w.head: θρηνέω
qrhne/w.html: θρηνέω [θρῆνος.] To sing a dirge, wail Il. 24.722: Od. 24.61.

qa/mnos.head: θάμνος
qa/mnos.html: θάμνος ὁ [cf. θαμέες.] 1 A bush, shrub, small tree: θάμνῳ ὑπʼ ἀμφικόμῳ Il. 17.677. Cf. Il. 11.156, Il. 22.191: δοιοὺς ὑπήλυθε θάμνους Od. 5.476, θάμνος ἐλαίης (consisting of . . .) Od. 23.190. Cf. Od. 22.469 2 In pl., a thicket: θάμνων ὑπεδύσετο Od. 6.127. Cf. Od. 5.471, Od. 7.285.

qessalo/s.head: Θεσσαλός
qessalo/s.html: Θεσσαλός Patronymic Ἡρακλεΐδης. Son of Heracles and father of Pheidippus and Antiphus-1 Il. 2.679 .

qnhto/s.head: θνητός
qnhto/s.html: θνητός -ή [θνη-, θνῄσκω.] 1 Mortal, liable to death Il. 1.339, Il. 10.403, Il. 13.322, Il. 16.622, Il. 21.569, etc.: Od. 1.219, Od. 3.3, Od. 11.244, Od. 12.118, Od. 20.46, etc. 2 Absol., a mortal man, a man: ἕνεκα θνητῶν Il. 1.574, τί δόμεν πηλῆϊ θνητῷ; (to Peleus, to a mortal) Il. 17.444. Cf. Il. 12.242, Il. 17.547, Il. 20.64: Od. 19.593. Fem.: θνητὰς ἀθανάτῃσιν ἐρίζειν Od. 5.213.

qersi/loxos.head: Θερσίλοχος
qersi/loxos.html: Θερσίλοχος Trojan. A Paeonian Il. 17.216 . Killed by Achilles Il. 21.209.

qermai/nw.head: θερμαίνω
qermai/nw.html: θερμαίνω [θερμός.] 3 sing. aor. subj. θερμήνῃ Il. 14.7. (ὑπο-.) To heat Il. 14.7: Od. 9.376.

qama/.head: θαμά
qama/.html: θαμά [adv. answering to θαμέες.] Often: ταῦτά με θ. ἐβάζετε Il. 16.207. Cf. Il. 15.470: Od. 1.143, 209, Od. 4.178, 686, Od. 15.516, Od. 16.27, Od. 19.521.

qhle/w.head: θηλέω
qhle/w.html: θηλέω [θη-, θάλλω.] (ἀνα-.) To teem with, abound in. With genit.: ἴου Od. 5.73.

qalpwrh/.head: θαλπωρή
qalpwrh/.html: θαλπωρή ἡ [θάλπω.] Warmth; hence 1 Comfort, consolation, cheering: οὐκ ἄλλη ἔσται θ. Il. 6.412. Cf. Od. 1.167. 2 Heartening, confidence: μᾶλλον θ. ἔσται Il. 10.223.

qla/w.head: †θλάω
qla/w.html: †θλάω 3 sing. aor. ἔθλασε Od. 18.97. θλάσσε Il. 5.307, Il. 12.384. To smash, crush: κοτύλην Il. 5.307, κυνέην Il. 12.384, ὀστέα Od. 18.97.

qeoei/kelos.head: θεοείκελος
qeoei/kelos.html: θεοείκελος (θεοϝείκελος) [θεός + (ϝ)είκελος.] Like the gods, godlike. Epithet of persons Il. 1.131 = Il. 19.155: Od. 3.416, Od. 4.276, Od. 8.256.

qh/rh.head: θήρη
qh/rh.html: θήρη -ης, ἡ [θήρ.] 1 Hunting, the chase: αἵμονα θήρης Il. 5.49. Cf. Il. 10.360: Od. 19.429. 2 The quarry: ἔδωκε θεὸς μενοεικέα θήρην Od. 9.158.

qeoeidh/s.head: θεοειδής
qeoeidh/s.html: θεοειδής (θεοϝειδής) [θεός + (ϝ)εῖδος.] Divine of form, godlike. Epithet of persons Il. 2.623, 862, Il. 3.16, Il. 12.94, Il. 17.494, 534, Il. 19.327, Il. 24.217, etc.: Od. 1.113, Od. 4.628, Od. 6.7, Od. 7.231, Od. 10.205, Od. 15.271, Od. 21.277, etc.

qrasu/mhlos.head: Θρασύμηλος
qrasu/mhlos.html: Θρασύμηλος Trojan. (ἀγακλειτός). Killed by Patroclus Il. 16.463.

qo/wn.head: Θόων-1
qo/wn.html:
Θόων-1 Trojan. Son of Phaenops-1. With his brother Xanthus-3 killed by Diomedes Il. 5.152.
Θόων-2 Trojan. killed by Odysseus Il. 11.422.
Θόων-3 Trojan. Il. 12.140. Killed by Antilochus Il. 13.545.
Θόων-4. A Phaeacian Od. 8.113 .

qi/sbh.head: Θίσβη
qi/sbh.html: Θίσβη (πολυτρήρων). A Boeotian town Il. 2.502.

qe/lgw.head: θέλγω
qe/lgw.html: θέλγω 3 sing. pa. iterative θέλγεσκε Od. 3.264. 3 fut. θέλξει Od. 16.298. 3 sing. aor. ἔθελξε Il. 15.322: Od. 10.318. Pple. θέλξας Il. 13.435. Infin. θέλξαι Od. 10.291. 2 sing. aor. pass. ἐθέλχθης Od. 10.326. 3 pl. ἔθελχθεν Od. 18.212. (κατα-.) 1 To work upon by spells or enchantment, bewithch, charm Il. 24.343: = Od. 5.47, Od. 10.291, 318, 326, Od. 24.3. Sim. of the operation of passion: ἔρῳ θυμὸν ἔθελχθεν Od. 18.212. 2 Of divine interference, to lay a spell upon, bind up from activity: Ἀχαιῶν νόον Il. 12.255. Cf. Il. 13.435, Il. 15.322, 594: Od. 16.298. 3 To work upon by wiles, cajole, lead on to one's hurt, prejudice, or dishonour: Ἀγαμεμνονέην ἄλοχον Od. 3.264. Cf. Od. 1.57, Od. 12.40, 44, Od. 18.282. 4 To beguile, deceive, cheat: δόλῳ [μιν] ἔθελγεν Il. 21.604. Cf. Il. 21.276: Od. 14.387, Od. 16.195. 5 To charm, delight, ravish Od. 17.521. In mid.: οἶα μυθεῖται, θέλγοιτό κέ τοι ἦτορ Od. 17.514.

qe/w.head: θέω
qe/w.html: θέω [θεϝ-.] Also θείω [prob. for θή(ϝ)ω, fr. θηϝ-, long form of θεϝ-.] 3 pl. pa. iterative θέεσκον Il. 20.229. 2 sing. fut. in mid. form θεύσεαι Il. 23.623. Infin. θεύσεσθαι Il. 11.701. (ἀμφι-, προ-, συν-, ὑπεκπρο-.) 1 Of men, horses, etc., to run, speed: θέεις ἀκίχητα διώκων Il. 17.75, ἵπποι βάρδιστοι θείειν Il. 23.310. Cf. Il. 2.183, Il. 4.244, Il. 6.54, Il. 15.442, Il. 19.415, Il. 23.387, etc.: Od. 3.112, 370, Od. 4.202, Od. 8.123, 247, Od. 14.501, Od. 17.308, Od. 22.99, 106. To run a race, contend in a race Il. 11.701, Il. 23.623. 2 Of the motion of a ship: νηῦς ἔθεεν κατὰ κῦμα Il. 1.483: = Od. 2.429. Cf. Od. 3.281, Od. 12.407, Od. 13.86, 88, Od. 14.299, Od. 15.294. Of a person in a ship: ὅτε κεῖνος ἐν νηυσὶ Μαλειάων ὄρος ἷξε θέων Od. 3.288. Of a rolling stone Il. 13.141. Of a δίσκος Od. 8.193. Of a potter's wheel Il. 18.601. 3 Of things, to run or extend: ἄντυξ ἣ πυμάτη θέεν ἀσπίδος Il. 6.118. Cf. Il. 6.320 = Il. 8.495, Il. 13.547, Il. 20.275: περὶ κλίσιον θέε πάντῃ Od. 24.208.

qh=lus.head: θῆλυς
qh=lus.html: θῆλυς [θη-, θάομαι2.] Also in regular fem. form θήλεια Il. 2.767, Il. 8.7, Il. 11.681, Il. 20.222: Od. 4.636, Od. 9.439, Od. 14.16, Od. 21.23. 1 Female: θήλεια θεός Il. 8.7, ὄϊν θῆλυν Il. 10.216. Cf. Il. 2.767, Il. 5.269, Il. 11.681, Il. 19.97, Il. 20.222, Il. 23.409: Od. 4.636 = Od. 21.23, Od. 9.439, Od. 10.527, 572, Od. 14.16. Comp. θηλυτέρη, female as opposed to male: θεαί Od. 8.324, γυναικῶν Od. 11.386. Cf. Il. 8.520: Od. 11.434 = Od. 15.422 = Od. 24.202, Od. 23.166. 2 Characteristic of women, feminine: θῆλυς ἀϋτή Od. 6.122. 3 Of dew, copious: θῆλυς ἐέρση Od. 5.467.

qa/muris.head: Θάμυρις
qa/muris.html: Θάμυρις A Thracian bard deprived by the Muses at Dorium of his power of song Il. 2.595.

qe/nar.head: θέναρ
qe/nar.html: θέναρ -αρος, τό. App., the palm of the hand Il. 5.339.

qa/rsunos.head: θάρσυνος
qa/rsunos.html: θάρσυνος -ον [θάρσος.] Having plucked up courage: Τρώων πόλις ἐπὶ πᾶσα βέβηκεν θ. Il. 16.70. Taking courage: θ. οἰωνῷ (from the . . .) Il. 13.823.

qe/meqla.head: θέμεθλα
qe/meqla.html: θέμεθλα τά [θε-, τίθημι.] 1 The root or bed (of the eye) Il. 14.493. 2 The lower part (of the throat) Il. 17.47.

qemei/lia.head: θεμείλια
qemei/lia.html: θεμείλια τά [as θέμεθλα.] Supports, consisting of stakes or stones, set to contain the face of an earthwork or mound (cf. στήλη 1) Il. 12.28, Il. 23.255.

qala/ssios.head: θαλάσσιος
qala/ssios.html: θαλάσσιος [θάλασσα.] Of or pertaining to the sea: ἔργα Il. 2.614: Od. 5.67.

qe/ros.head: θέρος
qe/ros.html: θέρος τό [θέρω. The hot season.] Genit. θέρευς Od. 7.118. Summer: θέρεϊ (in summer) Il. 22.151: χείματος οὐδὲ θέρευς (in winter or summer) Od. 7.118. As distinguished from ὀπώρη, early summerOd. 11.192, Od. 12.76, Od. 14.384.

qu/rh.head: θύρη
qu/rh.html: θύρη -ης, ἡ. Locative θύρηφι(ν) Od. 9.238, Od. 22.220. 1 a The door of a room: θαλάμοιο Il. 24.317. Cf. Od. 1.441, Od. 22.155, 157, 201, 258 = 275, 394. b In pl. (properly of a double or folding door; cf. Od. 17.267), the door of a house or room: ἐπὶ Πριάμοιο θύρῃσιν Il. 2.788. Cf. Il. 6.89, 298, Il. 7.346, Il. 9.473, 475, Il. 11.644, Il. 14.167 = 339, 169, Il. 22.66: προπάροιθε θυράων (i.e. the main door of the μέγαρον) Od. 1.107, θύρας ὤϊξεν (i.e. of the house) Od. 10.230. Cf. Od. 1.255, 436 (the same as the θύρην of 441), Od. 6.19, Od. 7.88, Od. 17.530 (outside), Od. 22.76, etc. Of the entrance to the cave of the Cyclops Od. 9.243, 304, 416, 417. To the cave of Scylla Od. 12.256. Of the entrances to the cave of the Naiads Od. 13.109, 370. Of the door of a pigsty Od. 10.389. 2 a The gate of the αὐλή: αὐλὴν ποίησαν θύρην δʼ ἔχε μοῦνος ἐπιβλής Il. 24.453. b In pl.: κληῗδα θυράων Il. 24.455. Cf. Il. 24.567 (the same as the θύρην of 453): ἔκτοσθεν αὐλῆς ὄρχατος ἄγχι θυράων Od. 7.112, αἰθούσης θύρας (see αἴθουσα (2)) Od. 18.102, ἐπʼ αὐλείῃσι θύρῃσιν (see αὔλειος) 239, Od. 23.49. Cf. Od. 1.120, Od. 16.344, Od. 17.267, Od. 21.191, 240, 389, 391, Od. 23.370. 3 In locative at the door. Hence, outside Od. 9.238. Out of doors, abroad: κτήματα, τά τʼ ἔνδοθι καὶ τὰ θύρηφιν (i.e. cattle, sheep, etc.) Od. 22.220.

qri/c.head: θρίξ
qri/c.html: θρίξ τριχός, ἡ. Always in pl. 1 The hair of the head: πολιὰς τρίχας Il. 22.77. Cf. Il. 23.135 (locks of hair): Od. 13.399, 431, Od. 18.355. The hair on the limbs: ὀρθαὶ τρίχες ἔσταν ἐνὶ μέλεσσιν Il. 24.359. 2 The hairs of the mane of a horse Il. 8.83. The hairs of a horse's tail Il. 23.519. The hair on the head of an ox Od. 3.446. Of the wool of sheep Il. 3.273. Of the bristles of swine Il. 19.254: Od. 10.239, 393, Od. 14.422.

qespidah/s.head: θεσπιδαής
qespidah/s.html: θεσπιδαής -ές (θεσπιδαϝής) [θε-σπ- as in θεσπέσιον (with the force of the second element lost) + δα(ϝ)-, δαίω1.] Epithet of fire, defying human efforts, devouring, consuming Il. 12.177, 441, Il. 15.597, Il. 20.490, Il. 21.342, 381, Il. 23.216: Od. 4.418.

qo/h.head: Θόη
qo/h.html: Θόη A Nereid Il. 18.40 .

qalu/sia.head: θαλύσια
qalu/sia.html: θαλύσια τά [θάλλω.] A sacrifice of first fruits: χωσαμένη ὅ οἱ οὔ τι θ. ῥέξεν Il. 9.534.

qi/s.head: θίς
qi/s.html: θίς θινός, ὁ. 1 The beach or shore of the sea: ἐπὶ θινί Od. 2.408. Cf. Od. 7.290, Od. 9.46, 551. The beach or shore (of the sea): παρὰ θῖνα θαλάσσης Il. 1.34. Cf. Il. 1.316, 327, 350, Il. 4.248, Il. 9.182, Il. 11.622, Il. 13.682, Il. 14.31, Il. 19.40, Il. 23.59, Il. 24.12: Od. 2.260, Od. 3.5, Od. 4.432, 779, Od. 6.94, 236, Od. 8.49, Od. 10.154, 179, 402, 407 = Od. 12.367, Od. 10.569, Od. 11.75, Od. 13.65, 220, Od. 14.347, Od. 15.205, Od. 16.358. App., a piece of the shore covered by shallow water: ὡς ὅτʼ ἀναπάλλεται ἰχθὺς θίνʼ ἐν φυκιόεντι Il. 23.693. 2 A heap: ὀστεόφιν θίς Od. 12.45.

qe/stwr.head: Θέστωρ
qe/stwr.html: Θέστωρ Trojan. Son of Enops-1. Killed by Patroclus Il. 16.401.

qeopro/pion.head: θεοπρόπιον
qeopro/pion.html: θεοπρόπιον -ου, τό [as θεοπροπίη.] = θεοπροπίη.: εἰπὲ θεοπρόπιον ὅ τι οἶσθα Il. 1.85. In pl. Il. 6.438.

qe/tis.head: Θέτις
qe/tis.html: Θέτις (ἁλοσύδνη, ἀργυρόπεζα , ἠΰκομος, θεά, καλλιπλόκαμος, τανύπεπλος ). Daughter of the ἅλιος γέρων (Nereus) Il. 1.556. Wife of Peleus and mother of Achilles. Comes when called upon by Achilles on his loss of Briseis Il. 1.357 , Achilles reminds her how she saved Zeus from bonds 396, she promises to induce Zeus to favour the Trojans 413, goes to him and gets his promise 495; received Dionysus when terrified by Lycourgus-1 Il. 6.136 ; the chest given by her to Achilles Il. 16.222; comes to Achilles on the death of Patroclus Il. 18.35 , promises him armour from Hephaestus 127, goes to Η. 369, how Eurynome-1 and she preserved Η. 398, she brings away the armour 616, and gives it to Achilles Il. 19.3; summoned by Zeus Il. 24.74 , and sent to bid Achilles release Hector's corpse 104, etc. : appears and takes part in the funeral rites of Achilles Od. 24.47, the jar given by her to receive Achilles's bones 73, the prizes given by her for his funeral games 85, 92.

qhn.head: θην
qhn.html: θην Enclitic affirmative particle: οὔ θην δηρὸν βέῃ Il. 16.852. Cf. Il. 9.394, Il. 11.365 = Il. 20.452, Il. 15.288, Il. 17.29, Il. 21.568: Od. 3.352, Od. 16.91. With mocking or ironical force: οὔ θήν μιν ἀνήσει θυμὸς νεικείειν Il. 2.276. Cf. Il. 8.448, Il. 10.104, Il. 13.620, 813, Il. 14.480: οὐ μέν θην κείνης γε χερείων εὔχομαι εἶναι Od. 5.211.

qaumaki/h.head: Θαυμακίη
qaumaki/h.html: Θαυμακίη A town of uncertain site in the realm of Philoctetes Il. 2.716.

qumoraisth/s.head: θυμοραϊστής
qumoraisth/s.html: θυμοραϊστής [θυμός + ῥαίω.] Life-destroying: θάνατος Il. 13.544, Il. 16.414 = 580. Cf. Il. 16.591, Il. 18.220.

qestori/dhs.head: Θεστορίδης-1.
qestori/dhs.html:
Θεστορίδης-1. Patronymic of Calchas Il. 1.69.
Θεστορίδης-2. Patronymic of Alcmaon-1 Il. 12.394.

qrasi/os.head: Θρασίος
qrasi/os.html: Θρασίος Trojan. A Paeonian. Killed by Achilles Il. 21.210.

qo/wsa.head: Θόωσα
qo/wsa.html: Θόωσα (νύμφη). A nymph, daughter of Phorcys-2 and by Poseidon mother of Polyphemus-1 Od. 1.71 .

qli/bw.head: †θλίβω
qli/bw.html: †θλίβω 3 sing. fut. mid. θλίψεται. To press or rub: πολλῇς φλιῇσι θλίψεται ὤμους Od. 17.221.

qala/mh.head: θαλάμη
qala/mh.html: θαλάμη -ης, ἡ [cf. θάλαμος.] A den or hole Od. 5.432.

qumodakh/s.head: θυμοδακής
qumodakh/s.html: θυμοδακής [θυμός + δακ-, δάκνω.] Biting the heart, stinging to action: μῦθος Od. 8.185. (Cf. δάκε φρένας μῦθος Il. 5.493.)

qumhgere/wn.head: θυμηγερέων
qumhgere/wn.html: θυμηγερέων [θυμός + ἀγερ-, ἀγείρω.] Endeavouring to rally one's spirit, making a fight for life: ἐκ δʼ ἔπεσον θυμηγερέων Od. 7.283.

qeo/qen.head: θεόθεν
qeo/qen.html: θεόθεν [θεός + -θεν 1.] From, at the hands of, the gods: θ. οὐκ ἔστʼ ἀλέασθαι [θάνατον] Od. 16.447.

qeoudh/s.head: θεουδής
qeoudh/s.html: θεουδής (θεοδϝής) [for θεοδϝεής fr. θεός + δϝ-, δείδοικα.] Acc. sing. θεουδέα (for θεουδεέα) Od. 19.364. God-fearing, reverencing the gods Od. 6.121 = Od. 9.176 = Od. 13.202, Od. 8.576, Od. 19.109, 364.

qemo/w.head: θεμόω
qemo/w.html: θεμόω [θε-, τίθημι.] To drive or carry in a specified direction: νῆα χέρσον ἱκέσθαι Od. 9.486, 542.

qrigko/s.head: θριγκός
qrigko/s.html: θριγκός ὁ. 1 An uppermost course in a wall, a coping Od. 17.267. 2 A frieze running along the upper part of the inner walls of a house Od. 7.87.

qureo/s.head: θυρεός
qureo/s.html: θυρεός -οῦ, ὁ [θύρη.] Something (in the passages cited a huge stone) placed to block up a door Od. 9.240 = 340, Od. 9.313.

qew/teros.head: θεώτερος
qew/teros.html: θεώτερος -η [comp. fr. θεός] Holy as distinguished from common: [θύραι] Od. 13.111.

qalpia/w.head: †θαλπιάω
qalpia/w.html: †θαλπιάω [θάλπω.] Pres. pple. θαλπιόων. To be warm: εὖ θαλπιόων Od. 19.319.

questia/dhs.head: Θυεστιάδης
questia/dhs.html: Θυεστιάδης Patronymic from prec. Of Aegisthus Od. 4.518.

qemisteu/w.head: θεμιστεύω
qemisteu/w.html: θεμιστεύω [θέμις.] 1 To pronounce judgments, act as judge Od. 11.569. 2 With genit. (like ἀνάσσω 3.a), to rule over, be master of: παίδων Od. 9.114.

qhmw/n.head: θημών
qhmw/n.html: θημών -ῶνος, ὁ [θη-, τίθημι.] A heap Od. 5.368.

qaumai/nw.head: †θαυμαίνω
qaumai/nw.html: †θαυμαίνω [as θαυμάζω.] Nom. pl. masc. fut. pple. θαυμανέοντες. To witness or watch with eager interest: ἀέθλια θαυμανέοντες Od. 8.108.

qeilo/pedon.head: θειλόπεδον
qeilo/pedon.html: θειλόπεδον τό [app. θείλη = εἵλη, the sun's warmth + πέδον, the ground.] A warm spot in a vineyard in which the grapes were left to be dried by the sun, a sun-trap Od. 7.123.

qoina/w.head: θοινάω
qoina/w.html: θοινάω [θοίνη, a meal.] To entertain at table: ἐς αὐτοὺς προτέρω ἄγε θοινηθῆναι Od. 4.36.

qumhdh/s.head: θυμηδής
qumhdh/s.html: θυμηδής -ές [θυμός + ἡδύς.] Pleasing to the heart, desirable, choice: χρήματα Od. 16.389.

qa/omai.head: †θάομαι1
qa/omai.html:
†θάομαι1 [θαϝ-. Cf. θαῦμα, θηέομαι.] 3 pl. aor. opt. θησαίατο. To admire, look at with admiration Od. 18.191.
†θάομαι2 [θη- as τι-θή-νη.] Non-thematic pres. infin. θῆσθαι Od. 4.89. 3 sing. aor. θήσατο Il. 24.58. 1 To suck (the breast): γυναῖκα θήσατο μαζόν (double acc. of whole and part, a woman's breast) Il. 24.58. 2 To suck (milk): παρέχουσι γάλα θῆσθαι (for their young to suck) Od. 4.89.

qa/lpw.head: θάλπω
qa/lpw.html: θάλπω To warm, to make flexible by the application of heat Od. 21.179, 184, 246.

qeoklu/menos.head: Θεοκλύμενος
qeoklu/menos.html: Θεοκλύμενος (θεοειδής, μάντις ). Son of Polypheides and great-grandson of Melampus. In flight from Argos-1 (1) encounters Telemachus embarking for home at Pylus Od. 15.223, 256, 271, is taken on board 286, asks as to his disposal 508, announces a good omen 529, is committed to the care of Peiraeus 540; his prediction to Penelope Od. 17.151; his vision among the suitors Od. 20.350, he leaves the suitors 363.

qerapeu/w.head: θεραπεύω
qerapeu/w.html: θεραπεύω [θεράπων.] To do service to, serve. With dat.: ᾧ πατρί Od. 13.265.

qesmo/s.head: θεσμός
qesmo/s.html: θεσμός ὁ [θεσ-, τίθημι.] Place, Site Od. 23.296.

qo/los.head: θόλος
qo/los.html: θόλος -ου. A building, app. of no great size, within the αὐλή, of unknown nature and useOd. 22.442 = 459, 466.

quw/dhs.head: θυώδης
quw/dhs.html: θυώδης [θύος (cf. θυήεις) + ὀδ-, ὄζω.] Sweet-smelling, fragrant Od. 4.121, Od. 5.264, Od. 21.52.

qhhth/r.head: θηητήρ
qhhth/r.html: θηητήρ [θηέομαι.] An admirer, fancier Od. 21.397.

qrigko/w.head: θριγκόω
qrigko/w.html: θριγκόω [θριγκός.] To finish off the upper part of the wall of (an enclosure) with something intended to give protection or to prevent exit: ἐθρίγκωσεν [αὐλὴν] ἀχέρδῳ Od. 14.10.

qe/spis.head: θέσπις
qe/spis.html: θέσπις [θε-σπ- as in θεσπέσιος.] = θεσπέσιος 2. Of song Od. 1.328, Od. 8.498. Of a singer Od. 17.385.

qrinaki/h.head: Θρινακίη
qrinaki/h.html: Θρινακίη Epithet or the name of the island containing the oxen of the Sun Od. 11.107, Od. 12.127, 135, Od. 19.275.

qh/s.head: θής
qh/s.html: θής θητός, ὁ. A labourer for hire Od. 4.644.

qalamhpo/los.head: θαλαμηπόλος
qalamhpo/los.html: θαλαμηπόλος ἡ [θάλαμος + -πολος, conn. with πολεύω.] A female servant in charge of the sleeping-rooms, a chamber-maid Od. 7.8, Od. 23.293.

qhreu/w.head: θηρεύω
qhreu/w.html: θηρεύω [θήρ.] To hunt, engage in hunting: ὥς μιν θηρεύοντʼ ἔλασεν σῦς Od. 19.465.

qa/lamo/nde.head: θάλαμόνδε
qa/lamo/nde.html: θάλαμόνδε [acc. of θάλαμος. + -δε 1.] To the θάλαμος (in sense (4)) Od. 2.348, Od. 21.8, Od. 22.109, 161.

qesprwtoi/.head: Θεσπρωτοί
qesprwtoi/.html: Θεσπρωτοί The inhabitants of Thesprotia, a part of Epeirus extending southeast from the Thyamis Od. 14.315, 316, 335, Od. 16.65, 427, Od. 17.526, Od. 19.271, 287, 292.

qallo/s.head: θαλλός
qallo/s.html: θαλλός ὁ [θάλλω.] Green stuff, fodder: θαλλὸν ἐρίφοισι φορῆναι Od. 17.224.
